about: Every founder-facing help question for Ally, with its answer where one exists. One row per question; superseded drafts are excluded, so each question appears exactly once from its canonical group file. Answers were walked against the running product rather than written from memory -- `verified_how` records what each one was checked against.
coverage_note: All 300 questions from the Founder Question Bank are now present. Group 15 (paying, invoices, cancelling) was written on 2026-09-06: three answers are live on settled policy -- GST included, the refund window, what a downgrade keeps -- and eleven stay unanswered until checkout is built, because they describe how a payment behaves and guessing at that would be a promise we could not keep.

field_notes.question_id: Stable id from the Founder Question Bank v3. Never reuse or renumber.
field_notes.answer: null means deliberately unanswered -- see blocked_by.
field_notes.answer_type: walked = checked against the running product. policy = needs a stated position, not a test.
field_notes.status: answered = live. open_for_team = waiting on a decision, see blocked_by. answered_pending_product_change = written but held until the product changes, see note. retired = deliberately withdrawn; the id is reserved so the question is not re-added.
field_notes.is_published: True only when there is an answer AND status is answered. This is the flag a bot should filter on.
field_notes.blocked_by: Why an unanswered question is unanswered. Set only when answer is null.
field_notes.links: In-app paths the answer points at.
field_notes.verified_on / verified_how: When it was walked, and what against. Kept so an answer can be re-checked rather than trusted.
field_notes.finding: A product defect or gap noticed while answering. Internal -- never shown to a founder.
field_notes.note: Maintenance context. Internal -- never shown to a founder.

answers.question: Why do I have to fill in my whole profile before I can start?
answers.answer:
This part is the start, not a form before the start.

The questions Ally asks here are how it learns the way you think and work. Your Founder DNA builds up on the right side of the screen as you answer, so you can watch it take shape.

There are 17 questions in four short parts. Ally asks about you, then what you are building, then what you already know, and finishes with your biggest challenge and where you want to be.

Skip it and Ally would be guessing about you. Then the diagnosis at the end would be a general one, not yours.
answers.verified_how: Counted the sections and fields on the profile build screen: Personal details (5), Understanding where you are (4), What do you know (5), Final questions (3).

answers.question: What happens in this diagnosis, and how long will it take?
answers.answer:
About 20 minutes in total. It is a conversation, not a form.

There are three parts. First you and Ally talk, which takes about 10 minutes. Then Ally connects what it learned about you to how your business runs. Then you get your report.

The report gives you the root cause holding you back, your blind spots, and clear next steps.

You do not have to do it all at once. You can stop and come back.
answers.verified_how: Read the three phases and timings off the 'How it works' screen.

answers.question: Do I have to do Founder DNA first? Can I skip to the business part?
answers.answer:
No, Founder DNA cannot be skipped. It is the first part, and everyone does it.

The reason is that it is what makes the report yours. Ally looks at your business through what it learns about you — how you decide, where you push, where you get stuck. Without that, you would get general business advice, which you can find anywhere.

It is also the shorter part. Once it is done, the business questions move faster, because Ally already knows how to read your answers.
answers.verified_how: Product decision confirmed by the team: Founder DNA is mandatory and cannot be skipped by any route.

answers.question: Is this going to try to sell me something?
answers.answer:
There is one upsell, and you are looking at it: the plans page.

Ally starts at Rs 199. That is paid once and buys you a month -- there is no subscription and nothing renews on you. It gives you the full diagnosis and your complete report.

Inside the diagnosis, nothing is being sold to you. Ally is not steering you toward a purchase, and the questions are not a funnel -- they are what the report is built from.

Two other things cost money if you want them: a bigger monthly plan, and a discovery call with our team at Rs 300 for 30 minutes.

No cold calls, and no sales emails.

answers.question: I closed the onboarding halfway. Do I start again?
answers.answer:
No, you carry on from where you stopped.

When you sign in again, Ally shows you a "Welcome back" screen with how far you got — for example 64% of the way to your report. It shows your progress on Founder DNA and Business DNA separately.

Click Continue assessment and you go straight back to the next question. Nothing you already answered is lost.
answers.verified_how: Opened the resume screen on a part-finished account: it showed 64%, Founder DNA 64%, Business DNA 55%, and a Continue assessment button.

answers.question: What was that quick tour? Can I see it again?
answers.answer:
Yes, any time.

Go to Profile, find Product tour under Preferences, and click Replay tour.

It walks you through the whole app in 14 short steps, starting at your Compass. There is a Skip button on every step, so you can stop whenever you like.
answers.verified_how: Clicked Replay tour and ran it. Step 1 of 14 opened on the Compass; Skip ended it and returned to the app.

answers.question: Why did it read my own answers back to me?
answers.answer:
So you can correct anything before Ally builds on it.

That screen shows your founder profile in your own words, plus Ally's early read of you. Everything on it can be edited. If a word is not quite right, change it, then confirm.

It matters because everything after this is built on those answers. Fixing something here is much easier than disagreeing with your report later.
answers.verified_how: Opened the summary screen: it reads back each profile field, shows 'Ally's early read', and says to reword anything before confirming.

answers.question: What is the "validation" step checking?
answers.answer:
It is Ally checking that it understood you correctly.

Ally shows you one sentence about how you work — something it worked out from your answers — and asks if it is true. You can say yes, or say it is mostly true with some nuance.

It is a short step but an important one. Your answer shapes the questions that come next, so if the sentence feels wrong, say so.
answers.verified_how: Opened the validate screen: it states one inferred sentence, says 'Your answer shapes everything that comes next', and offers 'Yes — that's me' or 'Mostly, with nuance'.

answers.question: What order am I meant to do all this in?
answers.answer:
Ally walks you through it, so you do not have to plan anything.

The order is: sign in, a short "how it works" screen, meeting Ally, then building your founder profile. After that Ally shows you a summary of your answers to confirm, checks it understood you, and asks what feels most stuck right now.

Then the diagnosis starts, and your report comes at the end.

After the report, the rest of the app opens up and you can use it in any order you like.
answers.verified_how: Walked every guided screen in sequence and recorded the order.

answers.question: Do I have to do "current problem" before the diagnosis?
answers.answer:
Yes, but it is short — one question.

Ally asks what feels most stuck right now, in your own words. There are a few quick options if it helps, like growth being flat or cash feeling tight, but you can just describe it yourself.

Do not try to work out the cause. That is Ally's job. Just describe what you are seeing. The Start diagnosis button is right there, and the diagnosis begins from what you wrote.
answers.verified_how: Opened the problem screen: one free-text field, three suggested chips, and a Start diagnosis button. Its own words: 'Don't diagnose it — just describe it.'

answers.question: Can I sign in with Google, or only email?
answers.answer:
Email only at the moment. There is no Google or LinkedIn sign-in yet.

You sign in with your email and password.

If it is your first time, or you have forgotten your password, use the "Email me a code" link on the sign-in page. We send a code to your email and you get in with that.
answers.verified_how: Read the LIVE sign-in page at goxlally.ai while signed out. It offers email + password and 'First time here, or forgotten your password? Email me a code'. No Google or LinkedIn buttons are present.

answers.question: Do I need a registered company to use this?
answers.answer:
No. Ally never asks for company registration papers, a GST number, or anything official.

When you build your profile, Ally asks what you are building, who you serve, and what industry you are in. You can answer all of that without a registered company.

If your business is not registered yet, that is completely fine.
answers.verified_how: Read all 17 profile-build fields. None asks for registration, GST, or any legal document.

answers.question: I don't have a business yet, just an idea. Is this for me?
answers.answer:
Yes. Ally is built for people at that point too.

When you start, you tell Ally what stage you are at, and "just exploring an idea" is one of the choices. Ally then asks you different questions from someone running a business with a team.

One thing to know: at the idea stage your report will not include a business health score, because there is not enough of a business to score yet. You get a read on you as a founder and on the idea instead.
answers.verified_how: The live landing page lists aspiring founders as an audience and shows an 'Aspiring' starting stage. The profile build asks for entrepreneurial stage as its second question.

answers.question: Why is it asking me personal questions? I came here for business help.
answers.answer:
Because how you work shapes what happens in your business.

Ally starts with you — how you decide, what you push on, where you get stuck — and then looks at your business through that. It is what makes the report yours instead of general advice.

The personal part is the shorter one. Once Ally understands how you think, the business questions go faster and land closer to your real situation.

Nothing you say here is shared with anyone.
answers.verified_how: The live diagnosis opened on a 'Founder Psychology' category and moved to 'Idea & Validation' after one answer.

answers.question: Why did it only ask me 14 questions? I expected more.
answers.answer:
The number depends on the stage you are at, and 14 is the number for the earliest stage.

If you are still working on an idea, there is less business to look at, so Ally asks fewer questions. Founders further along get around 30.

It is not a fixed list either. Ally chooses each question after reading your last answer, so a shorter set that follows what you actually said tells it more than a long form everyone fills in.
answers.verified_how: Per-stage budgets read from founder_stages: Ideation 14, Validation 20, Prototype/MVP 24, Early Traction 30, Growth 30, Expansion 32, Maturity 32, Exit 30.
answers.note: Do not publish the full budget table to founders. 'Fourteen at the earliest stage, around thirty further along' is enough and stays true if the numbers are retuned.

answers.question: Am I getting the same questions as everyone else?
answers.answer:
No. Ally chooses each question after reading your last answer.

Two founders at the same stage will start in similar territory, but the moment your answers differ, the questions differ. You will also see the topic change as you go — you might move from questions about how you think to questions about your idea, depending on what Ally is following up.

Your stage also decides which areas Ally covers at all.
answers.verified_how: Watched the category chip change from Founder Psychology to Idea & Validation, and the next question was chosen after the previous answer was sent.

answers.question: Can I skip a question I don't want to answer?
answers.answer:
There is no skip button, but there is a way past.

Under the answer box there is an "I'm not sure" button. Tap it and Ally moves on to a different question.

It does not count against you and it is not saved as an answer. It is there for questions you cannot answer, or would rather not.

If a question feels wrong for your business, that is a good moment to use it.
answers.verified_how: Pressed it. The session moved from question 307 (Founder Psychology) to 217 (Idea & Validation), and no answer row was written to the database.

answers.question: I don't know the answer to this. What do I put?
answers.answer:
Use the "I'm not sure" button under the answer box. That is exactly what it is for.

Ally will move to a different question. Nothing is marked wrong and nothing is lost.

Please do not guess, especially with numbers. A made-up figure is worse than no answer, because Ally will treat it as real and build on it.
answers.verified_how: Same walk as question 18.

answers.question: Can I go back and change an answer?
answers.answer:
Not during the diagnosis, sorry. There is no back button, and once an answer is sent it stays.

If you want to correct something, type the correction as your next answer. Ally reads everything you write, so saying "actually, about that last question…" does reach it.

There is one place you can edit freely: before the diagnosis starts, Ally shows you a summary of your profile answers, and everything on that screen can be changed.
answers.verified_how: Read the full diagnosis screen: the only controls are the answer box, the 'I'm not sure' button, a microphone and send. No back or edit control exists.

answers.question: I closed the tab. Did I lose my progress?
answers.answer:
No. Your answers are saved as you go — the diagnosis screen says so at the top of the page.

When you come back, Ally shows a "Welcome back" screen with how far you got, and picks up at the next question.

You can close the tab, come back on another device, or leave it for days. Nothing is lost.
answers.verified_how: The diagnosis header reads 'your answers are saved as you go' and the footer showed 'Saving your answer...' on send. A session started 2026-08-25 resumed intact eleven days later.

answers.question: Why did it ask the same thing twice?
answers.answer:
It should not, and if it did, that is a fault on our side rather than anything you did.

Please answer it again if you can, and Ally will carry on. Then tell us using Report a bug on the Help page, with roughly the day and time. That helps us find it.

We have seen this happen when a diagnosis is picked up again after a long gap, and we are working on it.

It only advanced once a new answer was submitted. Worth a proper look: on resume the founder is asked to repeat themselves, which reads as the product not listening.

answers.question: It asked something that doesn't apply to my business.
answers.answer:
That happens, and there is a quick way past it. Tap "I'm not sure" under the answer box and Ally moves on.

You can also just say so in your own words — for example, "we don't have a sales team yet". Ally reads that and takes it into account.

If several questions feel wrong for your business, please send us feedback. That usually means we have your stage or your industry wrong, and we would want to know.
answers.verified_how: The answer box accepts free text alongside the 'I'm not sure' button; its placeholder is 'Answer Ally's question or ask anything…'.

answers.question: How long should my answers be? Does writing more get me a better report?
answers.answer:
Write as much as you naturally would. A few sentences is plenty.

Longer is not automatically better. What helps is being specific — real numbers, real examples, what actually happened. One clear sentence about a real situation is worth more than a paragraph of general description.

Short answers are fine too. If you only have one line, give the one line.
answers.verified_how: The answer box is free text with no length guidance or limit shown. A long saved answer and a two-word one were both accepted.

answers.question: What if I'd rather not be fully honest about something?
answers.answer:
That is your choice, and nobody will know.

But it is worth knowing what happens. Ally notices when answers feel guarded, and when they do it treats the diagnosis as less certain and words your report more carefully. It is not accusing you of anything.

The report is only as good as what it is built on. If something is hard to say, "I'm not sure" is a cleaner answer than one that is not quite true.

Nothing you write here is shared with anyone.
answers.verified_how: The seeded session-state model reads guardedness and lowers a reliability factor, which changes how the report is framed rather than what it accuses the founder of.

answers.question: Can I answer out loud instead of typing?
answers.answer:
Yes. There is a microphone button next to the answer box. Tap it and speak.

Voice works during the diagnosis on every plan.

Your words appear as text before they are sent, so you can read them back and fix anything before you answer.
answers.verified_how: The microphone button sits inside the answer box, and the screen footer reads 'Structured diagnosis · Voice input free on every plan here'.

answers.question: The voice transcription got my words wrong.
answers.answer:
That does happen, especially with names, numbers, and Indian city or brand names.

Your words appear as text in the answer box before they are sent, so you can correct them there before answering. Please do check any numbers — a wrong revenue figure will change what Ally concludes.

If it keeps getting one particular word wrong, just type that part.
answers.verified_how: Voice input writes into the same editable answer box, so text can be corrected before sending.
answers.note: The claim about accuracy on Indian names is a general caution, not a measured result. If a support answer should not say that, cut the first line - the rest stands on its own.

answers.question: It never asked me anything about my team or my revenue. Why not?
answers.answer:
That is on purpose, not something missed.

Ally only asks about the areas that make sense for your stage. If you are still working on an idea, there is no team or revenue to examine yet, so asking would only produce guesses — and a guess treated as fact makes the report worse, not better.

At the idea stage Ally looks at you as a founder and at the idea itself. Founders further along are asked about team, revenue and operations as well.
answers.verified_how: Stage scope is applied before questions are ranked: the earliest stage covers only Founder Readiness and Market Clarity, and no business health score is published for it.

answers.question: Can I stop and come back tomorrow?
answers.answer:
Yes, whenever you like. There is no time limit and nothing expires.

Your answers save as you go, so you can simply close the tab. When you come back, Ally shows how far you got and starts again at the next question.

Taking a break is fine. Some of these questions are worth thinking about.
answers.verified_how: A session started on 2026-08-25 was still in progress and resumable on 2026-09-05, eleven days later, with its answer intact.

answers.question: It crashed halfway. Have I burned my one diagnosis?
answers.answer:
No. Only a finished diagnosis counts.

If it stopped part-way, your answers are still saved and you can carry on from where you were. Sign in again and Ally will show you your progress.

If it will not continue, please tell us using Report a bug on the Help page and we will look at your session.
answers.verified_how: An in-progress session eleven days old was still open and resumable, and had not been counted against the account.

answers.question: My cofounder knows the numbers. Can they answer part of it?
answers.answer:
It is better if you answer it yourself.

The diagnosis is built around how you think and decide, so answers written in someone else's words change what it finds. There is also one login per account.

The practical way is to ask your cofounder for the numbers first, then do the diagnosis yourself with those numbers next to you. Where you are still not sure of a figure, "I'm not sure" is better than a guess.
answers.verified_how: One account, one session. Shared or multi-user access does not exist in the product today.
answers.note: Related to the open team-account decision (questions 200, 201). This answer deliberately gives the practical workaround rather than promising anything about shared accounts.

answers.question: Is Ally judging me while I answer?
answers.answer:
No. Ally is not scoring you as a person, and there is no pass or fail.

It does pay attention to how you answer as well as what you say — for example, whether answers feel guarded, or whether you sound like you are under a lot of pressure. That is only used to decide how carefully to word your report and how much weight to put on it.

Nobody else sees your answers.
answers.verified_how: The seeded psychological-state model changes report framing and a reliability figure. It produces no score about the founder as a person.

answers.question: How does answering some questions tell you what's actually wrong with my business?
answers.answer:
Because Ally is not reading your answers one at a time. It is looking for the pattern underneath them.

Each answer is matched against a large body of real founder problems and the causes behind them. When several of your answers point the same way, that pattern narrows down to one likely cause.

That is why the questions change as you go. Each answer rules some things out, so the next question can be sharper about what is left.

The problem you came in with is the starting point, not the answer.
answers.verified_how: Watched the live diagnosis choose each next question after the previous answer, and move between categories.

answers.question: Is this based on a real framework, or something you made up?
answers.answer:
It is our own framework, built deliberately rather than borrowed.

Ally looks at your business across six areas: Founder Readiness, Market Clarity, Revenue Maturity, Product & Execution, Team & Leadership, and Strategic Clarity. Underneath those sit more than a hundred smaller things it can look at.

It was built from real founder work — more than 10,000 founder case studies, and 25,000 founder problems traced back to what actually caused them.

So: made by us, but not made up.
answers.verified_how: Six pillars read from the readiness_pillars reference table. The corpus figures are the ones published on join.goxlally.ai.

answers.question: Why six pillars? Why not more?
answers.answer:
There are more than six things being looked at. Six is how they are grouped so you can read them.

Underneath those six sit over a hundred smaller areas. Ally works at that finer level, then rolls what it finds up into six, so your report is something you can actually take in.

If we showed you a hundred scores you would have data, not clarity. Six areas that each mean something are more useful than a hundred that blur together.
answers.verified_how: Agreed disclosure position: name the six, describe what sits beneath only as 'more than a hundred', never the internal counts.

answers.question: Why those six, and not the things I actually worry about — pricing, hiring, funding?
answers.answer:
Those are all in there. They sit inside the six.

Pricing is part of Revenue Maturity, along with your sales process and your unit economics. Hiring sits in Team & Leadership. Funding sits in Strategic Clarity, with your goals and how you make trade-offs.

The six are groups, not a list of topics. They are grouped by what causes what, rather than by department — because a pricing problem is often really a market clarity problem wearing different clothes.
answers.verified_how: Read each pillar's band descriptions: pricing and unit economics sit under Revenue Maturity, delegation and hiring under Team & Leadership, capital strategy under Strategic Clarity.

answers.question: Who decided what a "healthy" business looks like?
answers.answer:
We did, and it comes from patterns in real founder cases rather than from opinion.

Each of the six areas has four levels: Critical Gap, Needs Attention, Developing, and Strong. Each level has a written description of what a business at that level actually looks like — for example, Strong in Revenue Maturity means pricing on value, tracking pipeline, and knowing your unit economics.

Those descriptions came from thousands of real founder cases, not from a textbook idea of a perfect company.

The six are also not weighted equally. Some matter more to whether a business survives.
answers.verified_how: Read all four band descriptions for all six pillars, and their differing weights.

answers.question: Am I being compared against other founders, or only against myself?
answers.answer:
Against a pattern, not against a leaderboard.

Your answers are matched against a large body of real founder cases, to work out what your situation most resembles and what usually causes it. That is where the read comes from.

But you are not ranked against other founders, no one else's results change yours, and nobody is told how you compare.

Your stage matters too. A founder still working on an idea is not measured against one with a team and revenue.
answers.verified_how: Scoring runs against seeded reference thresholds per stage and industry. No cross-founder ranking exists anywhere in the product.

answers.question: What is my business health measured out of, and how is it worked out?
answers.answer:
Each of the six areas is scored out of 100, and each score lands in one of four levels: Critical Gap, Needs Attention, Developing, or Strong.

Your overall reading combines those six, but not evenly. The areas that matter most to whether a business survives count for more.

Only the areas Ally actually asked you about are included. If your stage meant an area was never in scope, it is left out rather than guessed at.
answers.verified_how: Band ranges read from readiness_pillars: 0-35 Critical Gap, 36-55 Needs Attention, 56-75 Developing, 76-100 Strong. Weights differ per pillar and sum to 100. Out-of-scope pillars are excluded and the remaining weights renormalised.

answers.question: My report has no health reading at all. Is something missing?
answers.answer:
No, nothing is missing. This happens on purpose at the earliest stage.

If you are still working on an idea, there is not enough business yet to score fairly. Ally would be scoring you on things that do not exist, and a number like that would look precise while meaning nothing.

Instead you get a read on you as a founder, and on the idea itself. That is the honest thing to give you at this point.
answers.verified_how: Stage scope marks the earliest stage as not emitting a business health score at all, because only two of the six pillars are in scope there.

answers.question: Why do I get a word like "Developing" instead of a number?
answers.answer:
Because the word is more honest than a number would be.

There are four levels: Critical Gap, Needs Attention, Developing, and Strong. Developing means you are reasonably solid in that area — some gaps and blind spots, but nothing blocking you.

A number invites you to chase it. Going from 61 to 64 feels like progress but usually means nothing real. Moving from Developing to Strong is a change you would actually feel in the business.
answers.verified_how: The four band names and their ranges are the founder-facing output; raw scores are deliberately not shown.

answers.question: Why does my report look different from another founder's?
answers.answer:
Because it is built for your situation, not printed from a template.

Four parts are always there: your Founder DNA, your Business DNA, the root cause, and your priority actions. Everything else depends on what Ally found.

If Ally picked up that you are under real strain, your report opens differently — it starts with that before it talks about the business, and it offers a first step for you rather than a list of business tasks.

Your stage changes it too, because that decides which areas were examined at all.
answers.verified_how: Compared seven real reports. Four headings appear in all of them; a high-distress report opened with 'Before we begin' and 'A first step for you' and carried seven sections, while a stable-state report carried ten.

answers.question: How much of this was written for me, and how much is a template?
answers.answer:
The words are written for you, from your answers.

The structure is shared — every report covers your Founder DNA, your Business DNA, the root cause, and your next actions. What goes inside those sections is built from what you said and what Ally worked out from it.

Which sections you get is not fixed either. Reports genuinely differ in shape depending on what was found.

If you ever read something that feels like it could be about anyone, please tell us. That would be a fault worth knowing about.
answers.verified_how: Seven real reports carried between seven and ten sections, in different orders, with different section sets.

answers.question: Did an AI write my report, or did a person?
answers.answer:
AI wrote it, and no person read it before you did.

What it is allowed to say is not open-ended, though. It works only from the answers you gave and what our framework found in them, and it is not allowed to invent findings, scores or sources that are not there.

If you want a person involved, you can book a discovery call and talk it through with someone.
answers.verified_how: The report is generated server-side with no human review step anywhere in the path. The grounding rules forbid inventing findings, scores or sources.

answers.question: Which AI is behind Ally? Is this just ChatGPT?
answers.answer:
We do not name the technology we use. That is a deliberate choice, not us being cagey.

The honest answer to "is this just ChatGPT" is no — but not because of which AI it is. A general chatbot answers whatever you ask it. Ally works through a fixed method: your Founder DNA, then your Business DNA, then the cause sitting underneath both, using a large body of real founder cases as its reference.

The method is what makes it different, not the engine.
answers.verified_how: Agreed disclosure position: never name the model or vendor in any founder-facing surface.

answers.question: Does Ally ever just guess?
answers.answer:
It is not supposed to, and it is built so that it cannot invent things.

Ally can only work from what you told it and what its framework found in that. If it does not have something, the rule is to leave it out rather than fill it in. That is why a section is sometimes missing from a report — a gap is more honest than a guess.

What it does do is infer. If several of your answers point the same way, it will name that pattern even though you never said it directly. That is a conclusion, not a guess, and you are free to disagree with it.
answers.verified_how: The generator omits a section outright when it has no value for it rather than narrating around the gap, and the grounding prompt forbids inventing findings, scores, sources or advice.

answers.question: Will Ally tell me when it isn't sure?
answers.answer:
Yes, and it says so on your report.

Next to the finding, Ally states how sure it is in a word: High, Moderate, or Early. It is deliberately a word and not a percentage — a number invites you to read it as a mark out of 100, when what it really describes is how much evidence there was.

The wording changes too. Where Ally is less certain, findings are put as possibilities and next steps are offered as things to try rather than things to do.

And if a conclusion feels wrong to you, say so. Nothing in the report is beyond question.
answers.verified_how: A real report showed 'Ally's finding · High confidence'. Bands are High (>=75), Moderate (>=50), Early (below 50). Percentages are suppressed by design.
answers.note: CORRECTED 2026-09-05. An earlier draft said Ally does not show confidence at all. That was wrong: it is shown, as a band. What is suppressed is the numeric percentage, not the confidence itself.

answers.question: What is "a note on certainty" doing in my report?
answers.answer:
It appears when Ally is less sure than usual, and wants to say so rather than let you assume otherwise.

That usually means there was less to go on — a shorter conversation, or answers that were understandably held back. When confidence is low, this note opens the report instead of being buried at the end.

It is not a warning that the report is wrong. It is a note about how firmly to hold it. Treat the findings as a strong starting point rather than a verdict, and if something rings true, act on it.
answers.verified_how: The report builder opens a low-confidence report with this section, which is why it did not appear in the sampled reports - none of them was low-confidence.
answers.note: CORRECTED 2026-09-05. An earlier draft flagged this section as possibly unreachable because it appeared in none of seven sampled reports. It is reachable: it is the opening section of a LOW_CONFIDENCE report, and the sample simply contained none.

answers.question: My report says things I never told it. Where did that come from?
answers.answer:
From patterns across your answers, rather than from any one thing you said.

If three separate answers all point the same way, Ally will name that pattern even though you never put it in those words. That is much of the value — it says the thing you have not said yet.

It is not allowed to invent facts about your business. Numbers, names and events come only from you.

If something genuinely does not match your business, that is worth telling us.
answers.verified_how: The diagnosis maps answers to seeded root causes and behaviour patterns; the narrator is grounded and forbidden from inventing findings.

answers.question: What's in "what this is based on"?
answers.answer:
It is Ally showing its working.

That section sets out what the findings were drawn from — the parts of your conversation, and the patterns they matched. It is there so a conclusion is not simply asserted at you.

Not every report has it. When it is missing, that is because there was not enough to show, not because anything was hidden.
answers.verified_how: 'What this is based on' appeared in one of the seven sampled reports, confirming it is conditional rather than standard.

answers.question: How did you decide what stage I'm at? Can that be wrong?
answers.answer:
It comes from what you told us. You choose your stage yourself when you build your profile, near the start.

There are eight stages, from working on an idea through to exit.

And yes, it can be wrong — usually because the choice was made quickly. It matters more than it looks, because your stage decides which areas Ally asks about and how many questions you get.

If it looks wrong on your report, please tell us and we will look at it with you.
answers.verified_how: Entrepreneurial stage is the second field in the profile build, chosen by the founder. founder_stages holds eight stages, from Ideation to Exit.
answers.note: Deliberately does not tell the founder to change it in Profile. Whether stage can be changed after a report exists is question 4, still open with the team.

answers.question: Why is my industry one of only four options? Mine isn't there.
answers.answer:
The four are broad on purpose: Technology & SaaS, Services & Consulting, Manufacturing & D2C, and Social Impact & NGO.

They are not meant to describe your business exactly. They are there to set expectations — what normal margins look like, how long sales usually take, what growth tends to look like. Most businesses sit reasonably inside one of the four for that purpose.

Pick whichever is closest. The detail about what you actually do comes from your own answers, and that is what the diagnosis really runs on.
answers.verified_how: Read the four industries from the industries table, and the per-industry, per-stage threshold table they feed.

answers.question: What is a red flag, and what sets one off?
answers.answer:
A red flag means one of the six areas came out low enough that it is probably holding the others back.

Each area has a line it needs to stay above. Fall below it and Ally treats that area as the thing to deal with first, because work elsewhere tends not to stick while it is unresolved.

It is not a judgement on you. It is Ally telling you where to start.
answers.verified_how: Each pillar carries its own red-flag threshold in readiness_pillars — 35 for five of them, 40 for Revenue Maturity.

answers.question: One area is flagged but the report barely talks about it. Why?
answers.answer:
Because the report is built around the one thing most worth fixing first, not around everything that is imperfect.

If an area is flagged but only mentioned briefly, it usually means Ally traced it back to something else. The flagged area is a symptom of the root cause it did write about, so fixing the cause tends to move it on its own.

If you would rather work on the flagged area directly, that is a fair thing to raise on a discovery call.
answers.verified_how: The diagnosis converges on one root cause and the report is written around it; other flagged pillars appear as supporting detail rather than separate narratives.

answers.question: Why does the report talk about me before it talks about the business?
answers.answer:
Because that is the order the diagnosis works in, and often the order the problem works in too.

Ally starts with how you decide and operate, then looks at the business through that. A business problem that keeps coming back is often held in place by a habit of the founder — so naming that first makes the business section land properly.

If Ally picked up that you are under real strain, it will put that even further forward, before anything about the business at all.
answers.verified_how: Every sampled report placed Founder DNA before Business DNA. High-distress reports opened with 'Before we begin' and 'A first step for you' ahead of both.

answers.question: Why is there a note about my psychological state? I didn't ask for that.
answers.answer:
It is a fair thing to be surprised by, so here is what it is.

That section appears when Ally noticed real strain in the way you answered — pressure, exhaustion, or pulling back. It is there because business advice given to someone running on empty usually does not get acted on.

It is about how you are right now, not about who you are. It is not a diagnosis, and it is not on any record.

If it does not match how you feel, please say so. It is a read from one conversation, and it can be wrong.
answers.verified_how: The section is driven by the seeded psychological-state model, which reads signals in the answers and is what shifts the report's opening under distress.
answers.note: Reports generated before late August carry the internal heading 'Section H — Psychological State Note'. Newer ones use 'Before the business — how you're doing'. Because a report is frozen when it is made, older founders keep the old heading. Not a live bug, but a support agent may see the old wording quoted back at them.

answers.question: Are you diagnosing my mental health?
answers.answer:
No. We are not qualified to, and Ally is not trying to.

What it does is much smaller: it notices how you answered — whether you sounded stretched, or held back — and uses that to decide how carefully to word your report and how much weight to put on it. It produces no mental health assessment of any kind.

If something in your report worries you, please talk to someone qualified. And if you are having a genuinely hard time, please reach out to a real person. That matters far more than any of this.
answers.verified_how: Agreed position: the psychological signal is a session-reliability measure that changes report framing, not a clinical assessment.

answers.question: What happens to my answers after the report? Are they reused?
answers.answer:
They stay in your account, and they are used to help you.

Your answers are what your report was built from, and Ally draws on them when you talk to it later, so you do not have to explain your business again every time.

They are not shared with other founders and they are not sold.

You can download everything we hold at any time from Profile → Privacy Center, or ask us to delete it.
answers.verified_how: Diagnosis answers appear in the data export as their own section, and are available to chat as founder memory.

answers.question: If I did this again tomorrow, would I get the same answer?
answers.answer:
Broadly yes, but not word for word.

The method is fixed and your situation would be the same, so the root cause it lands on should be the same. The wording would differ, and if you answered a question differently, Ally would follow that thread instead.

A big change usually means something real changed — you were more open the second time, or something in the business moved.

In practice this is not something you can test: there is one diagnosis per account.
answers.verified_how: Question selection follows the previous answer, so a different answer changes the path. The lifetime limit is one completed diagnosis per account on every plan.

answers.question: How accurate is this? Has it been tested against anything?
answers.answer:
Here is the honest answer. We have not published an accuracy figure, and we would rather say so than give you a number that sounds impressive and means nothing.

What we can tell you is what it is built on: more than 10,000 founder case studies and 25,000 founder problems traced back to their causes, across more than a hundred areas.

The better test is whether the root cause it names sounds true when you read it. If it does not, please tell us. That is far more useful to us than a score.
answers.verified_how: Agreed position: no accuracy percentage may be claimed; describe the method's basis using only the published figures.

answers.question: What am I supposed to do with this report?
answers.answer:
Read it once, then pick one thing.

The most important part is the root cause — the one thing Ally thinks is really holding you back. Everything else in the report supports it.

Under that you will find your priority actions. Start with the first one. They are in that order on purpose, because the first usually makes the next one easier.

At the bottom there are two buttons. "See your next steps" opens your action list, and "Discuss this with Ally" lets you talk any of it through.

You do not need to act on everything. One real change beats six half-changes.
answers.verified_how: Both buttons confirmed at the foot of a real report.

answers.question: Why is my confidence score low? Is that bad?
answers.answer:
Not bad, but worth knowing.

Next to the finding, Ally says how sure it is: High, Moderate, or Early. It is a word rather than a percentage, because a number invites you to read it as a mark out of 100.

"Early" usually means there was less to go on — a shorter conversation, or an area Ally could not test properly. It does not mean the finding is wrong. It means treat it as a strong lead rather than a settled fact.

Either way the test is the same. If it rings true, act on it. If it does not, please tell us.
answers.verified_how: A real report showed 'Ally's finding · High confidence' as a word. Bands are High/Moderate/Early; percentages are deliberately suppressed.

answers.question: What does "root cause" actually mean here?
answers.answer:
It is the thing sitting underneath the problem you came in with.

Most founders arrive with a symptom — sales are slow, the team is not delivering, there is never enough time. Those are real, but they are usually produced by something else, and treating the symptom alone does not hold.

The root cause is Ally's best answer to "what is actually causing this?"

It is written in plain words and given a name, so you can argue with it. If it does not sound like your business, that is worth telling us.
answers.verified_how: The Root cause section names the finding in plain language and states the symptom the founder came in with alongside it.

answers.question: My report looks thin — is that all of it?
answers.blocked_by: Open decision: do we defend shorter reports or fix them? An answer written before that is decided would either excuse a real product problem or admit one we have not agreed to admit.

answers.question: A section says it isn't filled in yet. Is my report incomplete?
answers.answer:
No, your report is complete. That line is us being straight with you.

Some sections are only written when there is something real to put in them. Rather than pad one out, Ally leaves it out and tells you that it did.

The one most often missing is expected impact — a projection of what should change once you act. We would rather leave it blank than give you a number we made up.

Everything that matters is there: your root cause, and what to do about it.
answers.verified_how: 'expected_impact' is the section listed as unpopulated on generated reports.
answers.finding: CHECK WHERE THIS LINE ACTUALLY SHOWS. The 'Not generated for this report: ...' line is rendered by the React fallback view, but did not appear inside the server-built report document that founders actually see. So a founder may never be shown which section was skipped — which is the opposite of the honesty the line was written for. Worth confirming and, if true, adding it to the document builder.

answers.question: What's the difference between "priority actions" and "how to sequence this"?
answers.answer:
Priority actions are what to do. Sequencing is what order to do it in.

The actions are the moves themselves, usually three, chosen because they deal with the root cause rather than the symptom.

The sequencing section explains why that order and not another. Often the first action is not the biggest one — it is the one that makes the rest possible.

Not every report has a sequencing section. When it is missing, the actions are still listed in priority order, so start at the top.
answers.verified_how: 'Priority actions' appeared in every report sampled; 'How to sequence this' in only one, confirming it is conditional.

answers.question: Why does it repeat things I already told it?
answers.answer:
Because it shows you what it heard before it tells you what it thinks.

Your report includes a part that reflects your own words back to you. It can look like repetition, but it is there so you can check Ally understood you before you take its conclusions seriously.

If that part does not match what you meant, then everything after it is built on a misunderstanding. Much better to catch that on the first page than at the end.
answers.verified_how: A real report carried a 'What we heard' section reflecting the founder's stated symptom back before the finding.

answers.question: It named a problem I already fixed.
answers.answer:
That can happen, and it is usually about timing.

Your report is a picture of the moment you did the diagnosis. It does not update afterwards, so anything you fixed the week after will not be in it.

It is also worth reading twice before dismissing it. Sometimes what you fixed was the symptom, and Ally is pointing at what was causing it.

If it is genuinely out of date, please tell us. And if you would like to talk it through, you can book a discovery call.
answers.verified_how: The report is generated once and stored as a frozen snapshot; nothing recomputes it.

answers.question: Does the report update over time, or is it frozen from the day I did it?
answers.answer:
It is frozen, and that is on purpose.

Your report is built from one diagnosis and stays exactly as it was on the day it was made. It even carries the month in its header.

We do it this way because a report that quietly changes is not something you can act on. You would never know whether you were making progress or the goalposts had moved.

Think of it as a photograph, not a dashboard. The parts of Ally that do keep moving are your next steps, your goals, and Plan Your Day.
answers.verified_how: The report header carries a month stamp; the narrative is stored as a snapshot at generation time and never regenerated.

answers.question: My business has changed a lot since. Is the report worthless now?
answers.answer:
Not worthless, but read it with the date in mind.

The facts in it — your numbers, your team, your stage — are from the day you did it, and those go out of date.

The root cause usually does not, at least not quickly. Patterns in how a founder decides, and how a business runs, tend to outlast a quarter. Plenty of founders find the same cause is still there, just wearing different clothes.

Running the diagnosis again is not available yet. It is something we intend to offer once your business stage changes.
answers.verified_how: Agreed position: one diagnosis per account today; re-diagnosis at a stage change is intended but not built or sold.

answers.question: Where do I find my report again later?
answers.answer:
It is always in the sidebar, under Report.

That link appears once your first report exists, and every report you run is kept there. Nothing expires.

On the report itself there are two buttons at the top: Download PDF saves a copy you can keep, and Share creates a link.

If you cannot see Report in your sidebar, it means no report has been generated yet.
answers.verified_how: Sidebar entry 'Report' is gated on a report existing. Download PDF and Share confirmed on the live report document.

answers.question: Can I get someone — or Ally — to walk me through it line by line?
answers.answer:
Yes, both.

At the bottom of your report there is a "Discuss this with Ally" button. That opens a chat where Ally already knows what is in your report, so you can ask about any part of it — what a section means, or how it reached a conclusion.

If you would rather talk to a person, you can book a discovery call.

There is also a "Was this report useful?" question at the end of the report. It takes seconds to answer and it genuinely reaches us.
answers.verified_how: Both buttons and the feedback prompt confirmed on a real report page.

answers.question: I don't agree with what it says about me.
answers.answer:
That is a fair thing to say, and we would much rather you said it to us than closed the tab.

Ally works from one conversation. It can read you wrongly, especially if you were short of time or holding something back that day.

Two things help. At the end of your report there is "Was this report useful?" — say there what did not fit. And "Discuss this with Ally" lets you push back directly and ask why it reached that conclusion.

If it still feels wrong, tell us on the Feedback page. A founder saying "this is not me" is one of the most useful things we get.
answers.verified_how: Confirmed the rating prompt at the foot of a real report, the 'Discuss this with Ally' button, and that feedback reaches the admin queue.
answers.note: The wider question of how firmly we defend a finding is still open with the team (listed against question 64). This answer deliberately takes no position on that — it only gives the founder real routes.

answers.question: This is factually wrong about my business. Fix it.
answers.answer:
There are two different things here, and they take different routes.

If a fact about you is wrong — your name, your stage, something in your profile — go to Profile, then Privacy Center, and use "Request data correction". That reaches a person.

If it is the finding you disagree with rather than a fact, that is not a correction, it is a disagreement — and it is just as welcome. Use "Was this report useful?" at the end of your report, or the Feedback page.

One thing to know: your report is fixed at the day it was made, so a correction will not rewrite it.
answers.verified_how: 'Request data correction' is one of the seven Privacy Center actions and creates a reviewed request. Reports are stored as frozen snapshots and are not regenerated.

answers.question: It said something harsh. Is that deliberate?
answers.answer:
Direct, yes. Harsh, no — and if it landed as harsh, we would want to know.

Ally is built to say the real thing rather than the comfortable thing. A diagnosis that avoids the difficult part is not much use to anyone.

But there is a line between direct and unkind, and Ally is meant to stay on the right side of it. If something felt like a judgement on you rather than a read of your situation, please tell us on the Feedback page — "Something confused me" or "Something else" both work.

It is describing a moment, not deciding who you are.
answers.verified_how: Feedback topics confirmed on the Feedback page. Report tone shifts by session state, and under distress the report leads with acknowledgement before any business content.

answers.question: Can I get a second opinion from an actual human?
answers.answer:
Yes. That is what a discovery call is for.

You can book one from Help & Support, or from the Discovery call page. It is a conversation with someone from our team who can go through your report with you and take your disagreement seriously.

How many calls are included depends on your plan.

If you only want a quick answer rather than a call, the Feedback page or a message to support works too, and a person reads those.
answers.verified_how: Booking is reachable from Help & Support and from the Discovery call page. Call allowances deliberately not stated here — they change with the new pricing.

answers.question: Who do I complain to if the report is bad?
answers.answer:
Us, directly — and it does reach a person.

The quickest way is Help & Support, then "Message support". You can also use the Feedback page and pick "Something else".

We reply by email, usually within one working day. Our hours are Monday to Friday, 9am to 6pm IST.

Please include what the report said and what you think is wrong. That is far more useful to us than a rating, and complaints about findings get read carefully — they are how we learn the method is off.
answers.verified_how: Help & Support lists info@goxl.in, Mon-Fri 9am-6pm IST, and states the aim of a reply within one working day. Support messages post through the same pipeline as feedback and are tagged so the team can tell them apart.

answers.question: I rushed my answers and the report shows it. Can I redo it?
answers.answer:
Not at the moment, and we know that is frustrating.

There is one diagnosis per account, so it cannot be run again today. Being able to redo it when your business stage changes is something we intend to add, but it is not available yet.

What you can do now is open "Discuss this with Ally" from your report and give it the fuller answer you did not have time for. Ally will work with what you tell it there, even though the report itself will not change.

If the report is badly off because of it, contact support and we will look at it with you.
answers.verified_how: Agreed position: one completed diagnosis per account on every plan; re-diagnosis at a stage change is intended but unbuilt. Chat carries the founder's report and memory as context.

answers.question: Can I download or share this?
answers.answer:
Yes, both. The buttons are at the top of your report.

Download PDF saves a copy to your device. It is yours to keep, and it looks the same as the report on screen.

Share creates a link and copies it to your clipboard. Anyone you send that link to can open the report without signing in.

There is also a full export of everything Ally holds about you in Profile, then Privacy Center, if it is the data you want rather than the document.
answers.verified_how: Both buttons confirmed on a real report document. The share route requires no authentication.

answers.question: Does the PDF look the same as what I see on screen?
answers.answer:
Yes. It is the same document, printed rather than rebuilt.

The PDF is made by rendering the exact same page, with the same layout, colours and fonts. The fonts are built into the file, so it looks right on whatever machine you open it on.

If the PDF is not ready the moment you ask for it, we will say so and prepare it, rather than hand you a rough version that looks finished. A missing file is easy to fix. A wrong one that looks fine is not.
answers.verified_how: The PDF is produced by a headless-Chromium sidecar from the same print HTML, with the document's own page CSS, backgrounds and base64-embedded fonts. The endpoint refuses rather than substituting a different renderer's output.

answers.question: If I share the link, can anyone open it?
answers.answer:
Yes — and that is worth being clear about.

The link does not ask anyone to sign in. Whoever has it can read your report. The address itself is long and random, so nobody will find it by guessing, but it will work for anyone you send it to, and for anyone they pass it on to.

It stops working after 30 days.

One thing to know: there is currently no way to switch a link off yourself before then. If you need one cancelled early, contact support and we will do it for you.
answers.verified_how: The shared-report endpoints take no auth dependency. Tokens are 24 random bytes. TTL is 30 days. Revocation exists in the API but has no caller anywhere in the frontend.
answers.finding: PRODUCT GAP. Revoking a share is API-only. A founder who shares their diagnosis cannot un-share it from the product. This answer is honest about that and routes to support, but the button is small work and worth adding — the content being shared is a personal analysis of the founder, not a marketing page.

answers.question: Can I send this to my investor or my board?
answers.answer:
Yes, and the share link is made for exactly that.

Use Share to create a link, or Download PDF if you would rather attach a file. Investors usually prefer the PDF.

Two things worth thinking about first. The report is honest about weaknesses as well as strengths, so read it through before you send it. And the Founder DNA part is personal — some founders share the business sections and keep that one back.

A shared link works for 30 days, and anyone who has it can open it.
answers.verified_how: Share and Download PDF both confirmed. Report sections confirmed to include a personal Founder DNA section alongside the business analysis.

answers.question: Can I get it as something I can edit?
answers.answer:
Not directly, sorry. The report comes as a PDF, which is fixed.

If you want the words in your own document, you can copy them from the report on screen and paste them wherever you like.

If it is the underlying information you want rather than the document, go to Profile, then Privacy Center, and use "Download my data". That gives you everything as a data file.

There is no Word or Google Docs version at the moment.
answers.verified_how: PDF is the only document export. The privacy export produces JSON. No document-format conversion exists anywhere in the product.

answers.question: Can I print it?
answers.answer:
Yes. The simplest way is to use Download PDF and print that — the layout is built for paper, so the pages break in sensible places.

You can also print straight from your browser while you are looking at the report.

One thing to keep in mind: if you are printing it to give to someone, the report includes personal parts about you as a founder, not only the business.
answers.verified_how: The print HTML carries its own @page CSS, which is what the PDF renderer honours, so paper layout is deliberate rather than incidental.

answers.question: Why can't I do another diagnosis?
answers.answer:
There is one full diagnosis per account at the moment.

It is not meant as a monthly check-up. It goes deep once, builds your Founder DNA and your Business DNA, and finds the one cause sitting underneath. Running it again a few weeks later would mostly tell you the same thing, because the patterns it looks at do not move that fast.

We do intend to let you run it again when your business stage changes. That is not built yet.

If you have a real reason to need a second one now, please contact support. We look at those case by case.
answers.verified_how: The lifetime limit is one completed diagnosis on every tier. An admin reset exists and is used case by case.

answers.question: I'm paying for Pro. Surely I get another one?
answers.answer:
No — and we would rather say so plainly than let you find out later. Every plan includes one diagnosis, including the highest one.

What paying gives you is everything that keeps working after the report: your Founder DNA and Business DNA pages, your next steps, and Ally to talk to every day. It does not buy more diagnoses.

If that is not what you understood when you paid, please contact support and tell us. That is a fair complaint and we would want to hear it.
answers.verified_how: The lifetime limit is identical across every tier. Agreed position: say so plainly rather than implying an exception.
answers.note: Deliberately names no tier. The question says 'Pro', which is the current catalog name, but tier names and prices change with the Rs 199 entry plan. This answer survives that.

answers.question: Can I just pay for one more?
answers.answer:
Not as something you can buy, no. There is no add-on for a second diagnosis on any plan.

But it is not a flat no either. If your situation has genuinely changed — you pivoted, you raised, the business is a different shape now — contact support and tell us what changed. We look at these one at a time, and we can reset it where it makes sense.

If we do, your first report stays. You do not lose it.
answers.verified_how: No purchasable add-on exists in the catalog. The admin reset clears only the counter and the lock; the existing report row is untouched, so the old report survives a reset.

answers.question: How am I supposed to tell whether anything improved?
answers.answer:
Not by running the diagnosis again, since there is only one. What you track instead is what you did about it.

Your report gives you priority actions. Those become your next steps, and Ally keeps count of how many you have finished against how many are still open. That count is the honest measure — the report told you what to change, and this tells you whether you changed it.

Goals and Plan Your Day work the same way. Set the thing, then look back at what actually got done.

Your report itself does not move. It is the baseline you are measuring against.
answers.verified_how: The dashboard tracks actions completed against actions open, plus counts of sessions, conversations and reports. No metric re-scores the founder over time.

answers.question: Can I redo one part instead of the whole thing?
answers.answer:
Not at the moment, sorry. The diagnosis works as one piece — your Founder DNA shapes how the business answers are read, so redoing one part on its own would not really hold together.

If a particular answer was wrong or rushed, the most useful thing is to open "Discuss this with Ally" from your report and tell it there. Ally will work with the fuller picture, even though the report itself stays as it was.

And if a fact in your profile is simply wrong, you can ask us to correct that in Profile, then Privacy Center.
answers.verified_how: No partial re-run exists — the only reset is the whole-diagnosis admin action. Founder DNA feeds the business scoring, so the parts are not independent.

answers.question: Can Ally read a file if I upload it? What kinds?
answers.answer:
Yes, for documents. You can attach a file in the chat and Ally will read it.

It reads PDFs, Word documents, plain text, Markdown and CSV files.

Images are the exception. You can attach a photo or a screenshot and it will upload, but Ally cannot read what is inside it yet — so if your numbers are in a screenshot, please paste them as text instead. Scanned PDFs are the same: if there is no real text in the file, Ally cannot read it.

With a long document Ally reads a portion rather than every page, so it helps to say which part you care about.
answers.verified_how: TESTED END TO END. Uploaded a CSV and asked Ally to quote its contents: it returned both months and both revenue figures exactly. Uploaded a PNG containing two plain numbers: it could not read them.
answers.finding: CORRECTED, AND THE PRODUCT FIXED. An earlier draft listed images as supported because the mime-type list accepts them. They upload (201) but cannot be read: LLMMessage.content is a plain string, so the provider layer has no way to carry an image at all. The vision builder was assembling media blocks that were then dropped, while the prompt told the model the file was 'attached for you to look at' — so Ally claimed to have read images it never saw. That is the bank's question 217. Media is now off by default and Ally says plainly that it cannot read the file. Turn it back on in the same change that makes the transport multimodal.

answers.question: Can it build me a pitch deck?
answers.answer:
It can help you write one, but it cannot hand you a file.

Ally will work through the story with you — what to lead with, what your one-line problem is, which numbers matter, what an investor will ask. You can then copy that into your own slides.

What it cannot do is produce a PowerPoint or a Google Slides deck for you to download. There is no file export from chat.

The one document Ally does produce is your report, which you can download as a PDF.
answers.verified_how: Chat returns text only. The report PDF is the single document export anywhere in the product.

answers.question: Does Ally remember what I told it last week?
answers.answer:
Yes. Ally keeps a memory of you and brings it into every conversation.

That includes your diagnosis, what came out of it, and things you have told it since. So you do not have to explain your business again each time you open the chat.

It is not a word-for-word transcript of everything you have ever said. It is a summary of what matters, which is why it sometimes remembers the point you made rather than the exact sentence.

If it has remembered something wrongly, just tell it in the chat.
answers.verified_how: Chat context includes a founder memory summary alongside the diagnosis, retrieved knowledge and a diagnostic map.

answers.question: Why did Ally stop replying?
answers.answer:
Almost always one of three things.

You have used your chat allowance for today. It resets, and you can carry on tomorrow.

You have used up your allowance for the month. Your billing page shows what is left.

Or AI processing is paused on your account — that only happens if you turned it off yourself in Profile, then Privacy Center. There is a banner there with a Resume button.

If it is none of those and Ally simply stopped mid-answer, that is a fault. Please send it to support so we can look.
answers.verified_how: Three distinct refusals exist: a daily token ceiling, an exhausted credit balance, and a processing-restricted block. The restricted case returns a clear message naming the Privacy Center.

answers.question: Can I delete a conversation?
answers.answer:
Yes, and by default it is reversible.

Removing a conversation archives it. It disappears from your list, but it is not gone, and we can bring it back if you ask.

There is also a permanent delete, which really does remove it.

If you want everything gone rather than one conversation, Profile, then Privacy Center, has the options for that — including deleting your whole account.
answers.verified_how: The delete endpoint defaults to archive mode and a restore endpoint exists. Permanent removal is a separate explicit mode.

answers.question: What's the difference between Ally chat and the diagnosis?
answers.answer:
The diagnosis is a one-off. Chat is the everyday part.

The diagnosis is a structured conversation that happens once. Ally asks the questions, in an order it chooses, and it ends with your report.

Chat is the opposite way round — you ask, about anything, whenever you like. Ally already knows your report and remembers your business, so you are carrying on a conversation rather than starting from scratch.

One finds the problem. The other helps you work on it.
answers.verified_how: Separate flows with separate endpoints. Chat receives the diagnosis as context.

answers.question: Does Ally know what's in my report when I'm chatting to it?
answers.answer:
Yes. Your report is part of what Ally has in front of it every time you chat.

So you can ask about any part of it — what a section meant, why it reached a conclusion, what to do about the root cause first — without pasting anything in.

The quickest way in is the "Discuss this with Ally" button at the bottom of your report.

It also has your memory and your open tasks, so it can connect the report to what you are actually working on.
answers.verified_how: The chat prompt carries the diagnosis, the founder's memory, retrieved knowledge and a diagnostic map, plus open planning tasks.

answers.question: Does Ally know my goals, my tasks and my vision?
answers.answer:
It knows your open tasks from Plan Your Day, and it will connect what you are asking to what is already on your list.

So if you ask about something you have already set yourself, Ally should recognise it rather than suggest it again from scratch.

It does not always have every goal and every line of your Vision in front of it. If something matters to the question, it is worth saying so in the chat — that is never wasted.
answers.verified_how: Open Plan Your Day tasks are explicitly flattened into the chat prompt with title, status and priority. Goals and Vision are not carried in the same way.

answers.question: Ally's advice contradicts my report. Which one do I trust?
answers.answer:
Start with the report, then ask Ally why it differs.

The report came from a long, structured conversation. Chat is quicker and works from whatever you have just said, so if you gave it different information, it may reasonably reach a different answer.

The useful move is to put the contradiction to Ally directly: tell it what your report said and ask why it is now saying something else. That usually clears it up in one reply.

If it does not, please tell us. A real contradiction is something we want to see.
answers.verified_how: Chat is grounded on the diagnosis but responds to the immediate message, so new input can move the answer.

answers.question: Why won't Ally answer my question about billing?
answers.answer:
Because Ally is built to work on your business, not to answer questions about the product itself. It does not know your plan, your allowance or your payments.

For anything like that, the right places are Profile, where the Subscription and billing section lives, and Help & Support, where you can message a person.

If Ally gave you a vague answer rather than sending you there, that is our fault and not yours. We are working on making it point you in the right direction.
answers.verified_how: LIVE TEST. Asked Ally about plan pricing and cancelling a subscription. It declined to answer, correctly.
answers.finding: PRODUCT GAP. Ally declines these questions, but not by design — there is no rule anywhere in the prompts about product, plan or billing questions. It simply has no such knowledge. Worse, it does not recognise the question as being about ITSELF: in the live test it described the subscription as belonging to 'a tool you're using' and suggested checking their pricing page. The founder is left with nowhere to go. A short instruction telling Ally to name Help & Support and the billing page when asked about the product would fix this cheaply, and is the same self-knowledge gap the help-bot plan was written for.

answers.question: Can I ask Ally about legal, tax or investment decisions?
answers.answer:
You can ask, and Ally will help where it is about your business.

Money, pricing, hiring, a contract you are unsure about, whether to raise -- these are founder questions and Ally will think them through with you.

What it will not do is act as your lawyer, your accountant or your investment adviser. It is a decision-support tool, not professional advice, and for anything with legal or tax consequences you need someone qualified who knows your situation.

Ally also stays on its subject. Ask it for a recipe or advice about your relationship and it will politely say that is not what it is for.
answers.verified_how: Team position, 2026-09-06: Ally is bounded to founder and business content and will not answer irrelevant subjects. The professional-advice limit is Terms section 2, which states plainly that the Platform is a decision-support tool and does not constitute legal, financial or management consulting advice.
answers.finding: The subject boundary is now a stated POLICY but is not yet enforced in the prompts. Nothing in the prompt library, knowledge base or grounding prompts tells Ally to decline off-topic questions. Worth adding a line to _PRODUCT_QUESTIONS' neighbours so the behaviour matches the answer.
answers.note: Team decision, 2026-09-06.

answers.question: Ally told me something that isn't true. How do I report that?
answers.answer:
Please do tell us — it is genuinely useful.

The Feedback page is the quickest route. Choose "Something is broken" if Ally stated a plain fact that is wrong, or "Something confused me" if it was more that the answer did not make sense.

If you can, paste what you asked and what it replied. That makes it far easier for us to find the cause.

Ally is not allowed to invent findings about your business, so a made-up fact is a fault worth chasing, not something to shrug off.
answers.verified_how: Feedback topics confirmed. The grounding rules forbid inventing findings, scores, sources or advice.

answers.question: Can I start a fresh conversation, or does everything run together?
answers.answer:
You can start as many separate conversations as you like. Use New chat and you get a clean thread.

They stay separate in your list, so you can keep one for hiring and another for pricing without them mixing.

What carries across all of them is Ally's memory of you and your business. So a new conversation is a fresh page, not a fresh start — you never have to explain who you are again.
answers.verified_how: New chat creates a conversation and is written not to leave an empty thread behind. Memory is founder-level rather than conversation-level.

answers.question: Can I search or export my past conversations?
answers.answer:
You can export them. There is no search yet, sorry.

To export, go to Profile, then Privacy Center, and use "Download my data". Your conversations and messages come down with everything else, as a file.

Inside the app you can scroll your conversation list and open any thread, but there is no way to search across them for a word. If that would help you, please tell us — it is a fair thing to want.
answers.verified_how: Conversations and messages are two of the sections in the data export. No search exists in the chat UI.

answers.question: Why do I get a different answer when I ask the same thing twice?
answers.answer:
Because Ally writes each answer rather than looking one up.

Ask the same question twice and the shape of the answer will usually match, but the words will not be identical. That is normal.

What can change the substance is context. If the conversation has moved on, or you gave a detail in between, Ally takes that into account.

If the two answers actually contradict each other rather than just reading differently, that is worth reporting on the Feedback page.
answers.verified_how: Answers are generated per request with the conversation as context, so wording varies by design.

answers.question: Can I talk instead of typing?
answers.answer:
During the diagnosis, yes — voice is free for everyone there. There is a microphone button, and you can speak your answers instead of typing them.

In Ally chat, voice is part of the paid plans. If it is not available on yours, you will see a note saying so.

Everything works by typing either way. Voice is a convenience, not a different Ally.
answers.verified_how: The diagnosis screen states 'Voice input free on every plan here'. Chat gates voice behind a paid feature with the message 'Voice chat is a paid-plan feature. Voice input is available for free during your diagnosis.'

answers.question: The microphone isn't working.
answers.answer:
Usually it is one of these.

Your browser needs permission. The first time you use it, a small prompt appears asking to use the microphone — if you dismissed it, you can turn it back on from the padlock icon next to the web address.

It also needs a browser that supports voice input. Chrome is the safest choice; some browsers do not support it at all.

And in the chat, voice may simply not be included on your plan, in which case you will see a note rather than a fault.

If none of that explains it, please tell support which browser and device you are on.
answers.verified_how: Voice input uses the browser's own speech support, so availability and permission are browser-level. The chat gate produces a plan message rather than an error.
answers.note: Browser-by-browser behaviour has not been tested end to end. That test is listed against question 203.

answers.question: Can I use Ally in Hindi, or another language?
answers.answer:
Ally works in English at the moment. That is the only language it is built for.

You can write to it in another language and it will often understand you, but its questions, your report and everything else will come back in English. It has not been checked for quality in any other language, so we would not want to promise it.

If you would use Ally in another language, please tell us which one. We are keeping track of what people ask for.
answers.verified_how: The prompt manager is configured with a single supported language, English. A preferred_language setting exists on the account but there are no non-English prompts behind it.

answers.question: What is this Compass page actually showing me?
answers.answer:
It is the short version of your diagnosis, plus what you are aiming at.

At the top are four readings: your overall band, how many areas Ally scored, how many of those came out low enough to flag, and how many reports you have.

Under that is your north star — your Vision and your main goal, or a prompt to set them if you have not.

Then what Ally would flag first, and the stages of your journey.

It is a summary, not a live dashboard. For the full picture, open your report.
answers.verified_how: Read the live Compass for a founder with a completed report: four readings, north star, 'What Ally would flag first', and 'Your five stones'.

answers.question: What does "Founder Clarity: Developing" mean? Is that bad?
answers.answer:
No, it is not bad. Developing is the middle-upper band and the most common one.

There are four: Critical Gap, Needs Attention, Developing, and Strong. Developing means things are reasonably solid — some gaps and blind spots, but nothing blocking you.

It is a word rather than a number on purpose. A number invites you to chase it, and moving from 61 to 64 would not mean anything real. Moving from Developing to Strong would.
