It comes from your latest diagnosis. Your report explains what sits behind it.
answers.verified_how: Band names and ranges read from the pillar reference data: Critical Gap 0-35, Needs Attention 36-55, Developing 56-75, Strong 76-100. The Compass renders the band word, never the score.

answers.question: It says 0 red flags. Does that mean nothing's wrong?
answers.answer:
It means nothing came out low enough to be treated as urgent. That is genuinely good news, but it is not the same as nothing being wrong.

A red flag is Ally saying one area is bad enough that it is probably holding the others back. Zero of them means no area crossed that line.

You can still have plenty to work on. Your report will name the root cause and your priority actions whether or not anything was flagged.

So read zero red flags as "nothing is on fire", not as "nothing to do".
answers.verified_how: Red flags on the Compass is a count of pillars below their own threshold. The subtext reads 'None detected' at zero and 'Needs attention' otherwise.

answers.question: What is Journey? Why is it locked?
answers.answer:
It is not locked — it is not built yet, and the page says so.

Journey is meant to hold the path that shaped how you build: the decisions, lessons and turning points Ally picks up from your story over time. Open it today and you get an honest "coming soon" rather than a locked door.

So there is nothing you need to do to unlock it, and no plan that includes it yet. It will appear when it is ready.

In the meantime, your report and your Founder DNA page cover most of what Journey will eventually show.
answers.verified_how: The nav entry is flagged coming-soon rather than report-gated, and the page renders its own 'Coming soon' panel. Nothing gates it on a plan or a report.

answers.question: How do I unlock achievements?
answers.answer:
By talking to Ally. Achievements open up after 15 messages.

The page shows you exactly where you are — for example "You're at 6 of 15 messages" — with a progress bar, so you are never guessing.

It works that way because achievements come from what Ally learns about you in conversation. Before there is enough of your story, they would not mean anything.

There is no payment involved and nothing to claim. Just carry on using Ally and it opens by itself.
answers.verified_how: The unlock threshold is 15 messages, enforced server-side rather than in the UI. The gate renders live progress against it.

answers.question: My clarity number changed and I didn't do anything. Why?
answers.answer:
Your band should not change on its own. It comes from your diagnosis, and your diagnosis does not get re-run or re-scored in the background.

Two things on the Compass do move without you doing anything to your diagnosis: the report count, and the number of sessions underneath it.

If the band itself genuinely changed — say from Developing to Needs Attention — that is not expected, and we would want to know. Please tell support what it said before and what it says now.

Everything else on the page reflects the day you did your diagnosis.
answers.verified_how: The Compass reads the stored report. Reports are frozen snapshots and nothing recomputes them, so the band is fixed while counts can change.

answers.question: What is "AI sessions" counting?
answers.answer:
There is no AI sessions reading on the Compass, so this may be from an older version or another product — sorry for the confusion.

What you will see is a Reports count, with the number of completed sessions written underneath it. A session means one full run of the diagnosis, so for most founders that number is one.

The other three readings are your overall band, how many areas Ally scored, and how many were flagged.

If you are looking at something that does say "AI sessions", please send us a screenshot — we would like to see where it is.
answers.verified_how: 'AI Sessions' exists only in the frontend's mock-data file, which no page imports for these readings. The live Compass shows Founder clarity, Dimensions scanned, Red flags and Reports.

answers.question: Do achievements get me anything, or are they just badges?
answers.answer:
They are for you, not for us. There is no discount, no extra allowance and no unlock behind them.

They are a record of what you have actually done and what Ally has learned about you along the way. Founder work is long and quiet, and it is easy to forget how far you have come — that is what they are for.

You can add your own as well, and edit or remove any of them.

If you would rather they did something more, tell us. Nobody has decided that they never will.
answers.verified_how: Achievements are founder-editable records with create, edit and delete. Nothing in the plan catalog or the feature gates references them.

answers.question: Is any of this live, or is it all from the day I did the diagnosis?
answers.answer:
Mostly from the day you did your diagnosis, and the page says so — three of the four readings carry the line "From your latest diagnosis".

What does move: your report count, your completed sessions, your Vision and goals when you edit them, and your tasks in Plan Your Day.

What does not move: your band, the areas scored, and the red flags. Those are fixed to your diagnosis, and there is one diagnosis per account.

So treat the Compass as a summary you can come back to, and Plan Your Day as the part that tracks what you are doing now.
answers.verified_how: Three readings render the subtext 'From your latest diagnosis'. The north-star panel reads live Vision and goals. Reports and sessions come from live counts.

answers.question: What is my Founder DNA and what am I supposed to do with it?
answers.answer:
It is Ally's read of how you work — how you decide, what drives you, where you tend to get stuck.

The page has three parts: how you operate, your motivation and archetype, and your vision. The archetype is matched from your own words in the diagnosis, and it shows you which words it matched on.

What to do with it: read it once, and notice what you recognise. It is most useful as a lens on the business problem rather than on its own — the same constraint that shows up in how you work usually shows up in the company too.

It is not a label, and nobody else sees it.
answers.verified_how: Read the live Founder DNA page: hero, 'How you operate', 'Motivation & archetype' with matched terms, and 'Your vision'.

answers.question: Can I redo Founder DNA if I answered badly?
answers.answer:
Not on its own, sorry. Founder DNA comes out of the diagnosis, and there is one diagnosis per account.

It also could not really be redone by itself. What Ally learns about you is what it reads your business answers through, so changing one without the other would leave the two halves disagreeing.

What helps now: open Ally chat and tell it what you would have said. It will work with the fuller picture from then on, even though the page itself stays as it is.

If your answers were badly off, contact support and we will look at it with you.
answers.verified_how: No partial re-run exists. The only reset is a whole-diagnosis admin action, used case by case.

answers.question: What's Business DNA, and how is it different from Founder DNA?
answers.answer:
Founder DNA is about you. Business DNA is about the company.

Business DNA scores your business across six areas: Founder Readiness, Market Clarity, Revenue Maturity, Product & Execution, Team & Leadership, and Strategic Clarity. Each one lands in a band — Critical Gap, Needs Attention, Developing or Strong.

Founder DNA is how you decide and operate. Business DNA is how the business currently runs.

The point of having both is what sits between them. Ally looks for the place where a pattern of yours and a weakness in the business meet, and that is usually the root cause.
answers.verified_how: Pillar names and band names read from the reference data. The Business DNA page renders 'Business dimensions'.

answers.question: Why is Business DNA locked?
answers.answer:
Because it is built from your diagnosis, and there is nothing to show before you have done one.

It is not a paid feature and there is nothing to buy. Finish the diagnosis and both Business DNA and Founder DNA open up, along with your report.

If you have already finished a diagnosis and it still looks locked, that is a fault rather than a setting. Please tell support.
answers.verified_how: The sidebar gates Founder DNA and Business DNA on a report existing. Neither appears in the plan catalog's feature gates as a paid item.

answers.question: What's Vision for? Do I have to fill it in?
answers.answer:
No, it is completely optional. Nothing is blocked if you leave it empty.

Vision is a place to write down where you are actually trying to get to, across six areas: your life, the business, the impact you want, the financial picture, your ideal day, and what you want to leave behind. Each one takes a sentence or two, and you can add a picture.

What you write shows on your Compass as your north star, so it is in front of you rather than in a document you never open.

It is for you. It is not scored and nobody else sees it.
answers.verified_how: Six territory keys confirmed: life, business, impact, financial, ideal_day, legacy — each with a statement, two tags and an optional image, plus a summary. The Compass north-star panel reads it.

answers.question: Does Ally actually use my vision, or is it just for me to look at?
answers.answer:
Honest answer: mostly the second, for now.

When you chat with Ally it does not read your Vision page. It works from your diagnosis, what it remembers about you, your open tasks, and the profile you filled in at the start — which does include the one-year vision and 90-day goal you gave then.

So Ally knows roughly where you said you were heading. It does not see the six areas you wrote on the Vision page.

If your vision matters to a question, say it in the chat and Ally will use it. And we would like to close this gap — it is a fair thing to expect.
answers.verified_how: Traced the whole chat context assembly. It injects memory, retrieval, a diagnostic map, attachments, open plan tasks and an onboarding profile brief. That brief carries current challenges, the 90-day goal and the one-year vision. Nothing reads vision_territories or vision_summary.
answers.finding: PRODUCT GAP. The Vision page is the fullest statement a founder ever writes about where they are trying to get to, and the AI meant to help them get there never sees it. Same for Goals. Worth including in whatever change next widens chat context.

answers.question: Founder DNA is in my report and it's also a page. What's the difference?
answers.answer:
Same source, two different jobs.

The section in your report is the short version, written as part of the diagnosis and fixed to the day it was made. It is there because the rest of the report is built on it.

The page is the fuller view you can come back to — how you operate, your motivation and archetype, and your vision, laid out to read rather than to support an argument.

Neither changes on its own. If they ever disagree, please tell us, because they should not.
answers.verified_how: The Founder DNA page hero takes its heading from the report's own Founder DNA section, then adds the operating, archetype and vision panels.

answers.question: We've pivoted. Can I change my Business DNA?
answers.answer:
Not directly, no. Business DNA comes from your diagnosis, and it stays as it was on the day you did it.

That is worth knowing rather than working around: after a real pivot, the scores describe the business you used to have. Read them with the date in mind.

Running the diagnosis again after a change of stage is something we intend to add, but it is not available yet.

What you can do now is tell Ally in the chat what changed. It will work from that going forward. And if the pivot was large, contact support and we will look at your case.
answers.verified_how: Business DNA is stored on the report, which is a frozen snapshot. One diagnosis per account on every plan.

answers.question: Is Founder DNA a personality test? Which one is it based on?
answers.answer:
No, and it is not based on any of the well-known ones.

There is no questionnaire scored against a published personality model, and you will not get a four-letter type. Ally reads what you actually wrote about your own situation during the diagnosis and looks for patterns in it.

The archetype it shows you is matched from your own words — the page even lists which words it matched on, so you can see where it came from.

So treat it as a read of how you were working at that moment, not a fixed type. If it does not sound like you, say so.
answers.verified_how: The archetype card states 'from your own words in the diagnosis' and renders the matched terms. Nothing in the product references an external personality instrument.

answers.question: What's the difference between Goals and Plan Your Day?
answers.answer:
Goals are what you are trying to achieve. Plan Your Day is what you are doing about it today.

A goal is bigger and slower — grow revenue, hire a second engineer, get to a repeatable sales process. It sits there while you work towards it.

Plan Your Day is the short list of actual tasks, with times if you want them. It is where the work happens.

Most founders set a handful of goals and rarely change them, then live in Plan Your Day. If you only look at one, look at that one.
answers.verified_how: Separate features with separate storage: goals hold outcomes, planning holds dated tasks with status.

answers.question: Does Ally know about my goals when I'm talking to it?
answers.answer:
It knows your open tasks from Plan Your Day, and it will connect what you are asking to something already on your list.

It does not currently read your Goals page. So if a goal matters to what you are asking, mention it in the chat — Ally will use it straight away, it just will not have picked it up on its own.

It also knows the 90-day goal and one-year vision you gave during onboarding, because those were part of your profile.

We would like to close this gap. It is a fair thing to expect.
answers.verified_how: Traced the chat context: open plan tasks are injected with title, status and priority. Nothing reads the goals tables. The onboarding brief does carry the 90-day goal and one-year vision.

answers.question: Where do my recommendations come from? Did a person write these?
answers.answer:
They come from your diagnosis. No person wrote them for you.

They are part of your report — the same analysis, shown on their own page so you can work through them without opening the whole document.

So they are specific to what Ally found in your answers, not a general list of good advice. If a recommendation does not match your business, that is worth telling us, because it means the finding behind it may be off.

If you want a person involved, you can book a discovery call and go through them together.
answers.verified_how: Recommendations are served as a section of the report itself, generated from the diagnosis with no human review step anywhere in the path.

answers.question: Why do I only have two or three recommendations?
answers.answer:
Because that is the most you can actually act on, and because Ally would rather give you three real ones than six padded ones.

The plan is built as up to three moves to confirm what is really going on, and up to three to fix it. That is a ceiling, not a target — if only two are worth doing, you get two.

It is deliberate. A list of ten actions reads as thorough and gets nothing done. Three ordered ones, where the first makes the second easier, usually do.

Start at the top and work down.
answers.verified_how: The action plan is capped at three confirm/isolate actions and three solve actions, explicitly documented as a ceiling rather than a quota.

answers.question: What's the difference between recommendations and next steps?
answers.answer:
Same advice, two different views.

Recommendations are the thinking — what Ally suggests and why, straight from your diagnosis.

Next steps is the working list. It is where you actually pick things up, tick them off, and see what is left.

So read Recommendations once to understand the reasoning, then live in Next steps. And when you commit to doing something on a particular day, put it in Plan Your Day — that is the list that runs your week.
answers.verified_how: Both are gated on a report existing and both trace back to the same diagnosis output.

answers.question: What are frameworks and how do I actually use one?
answers.answer:
They are short, practical thinking tools — ten of them, each for a particular kind of decision.

Open one and you get the idea explained plainly, with how to apply it. There is a space for your own notes underneath, so you can write what it means for your business. Those notes are yours and Ally never writes them for you.

The useful way to use one is with a real decision in front of you rather than as reading. Pick the one that matches what you are stuck on, work your problem through it, and write down what came out.

Ally remembers which ones you have opened.
answers.verified_how: Ten frameworks in the library. Per-founder usage records last-opened and the founder's own note, explicitly never AI-written.

answers.question: Are the frameworks picked for me, or does everyone see the same ones?
answers.answer:
Everyone sees the same ten. They are a library, not a recommendation.

What is personal is what you do with them — which ones you have opened, when, and the notes you have written on each.

So nothing here is chosen for you based on your diagnosis. If you want to know which one fits your situation, ask Ally in the chat — it knows your report and can point you at the right one.

If frameworks picked for you would be more useful, tell us. It is a reasonable thing to want.
answers.verified_how: The framework list is a fixed set of ten shipped with the app, identical for every founder. Only usage and notes are per-founder.

answers.question: What's the difference between a task and a goal?
answers.answer:
A task is one thing you do. A goal is what all those things add up to.

"Call five customers this week" is a task. "Understand why people churn" is a goal.

Tasks live in Plan Your Day, can have a time on them, and get ticked off. Goals live on the Goals page and stay put while you work towards them.

If you are not sure which something is, ask whether you could finish it in a sitting. If yes, it is a task.
answers.verified_how: Tasks carry a status and an optional time and are completed; goals are outcomes without completion mechanics.

answers.question: Can I set a time for a task, and will I get a reminder?
answers.answer:
You can set a time, yes. The reminder is the weaker half.

Ally will nudge you inside the app about anything due or overdue. But it does not email you and there are no phone notifications, so if Ally is closed, nothing reaches you.

If you have connected a calendar, your tasks go onto it — and then your calendar reminds you, which works whether Ally is open or not. That is the most reliable option today.

We know in-app-only is a real limitation and we would like to fix it.
answers.verified_how: Nudges are computed client-side from due and overdue tasks. Only discovery-call notifications send email. Connected calendars receive a real event push.

answers.question: There are four different lists telling me what to do. Which is the real one?
answers.answer:
Plan Your Day. That is the one to work from.

Here is how the others relate to it. Your report names the priority actions — that is the thinking. Recommendations is the same advice on its own page. Next steps is the working list of those actions.

When you decide you are actually going to do something, put it in Plan Your Day with a day and a time. That is the only list built for doing rather than reading.

So: report to understand, Next steps to choose, Plan Your Day to work.
answers.verified_how: Settled position: Plan Your Day is the founder's real to-do list; the other surfaces feed it.

answers.question: What happens when I tick something off? Does anything update?
answers.answer:
Yes. Your completed count goes up and the task leaves your open list.

That count is how progress is actually measured in Ally. Your report is fixed at the day you made it, so it does not move — what moves is how many of its actions you have done. Your Compass reflects that.

What does not happen: your bands do not change, and nothing gets re-scored. Ticking off a task is a record of work done, not a new diagnosis.

So it is worth ticking things off honestly rather than tidily.
answers.verified_how: The dashboard tracks actions_open against actions_completed. Nothing recomputes report bands from task completion.

answers.question: Will Ally hold me to this? Does it check in?
answers.answer:
Only while you are in the app, and honestly that is a limitation.

When you open Ally, it will nudge you about anything overdue or due today. If you have connected a calendar, your tasks are on it and it will remind you properly.

What Ally will not do is chase you. It does not email you, it will not message you, and it cannot notice on a Thursday that you have not opened it since Monday.

So the accountability has to come from you opening it. If you would like Ally to check in properly, tell us — you would not be the first to ask.
answers.verified_how: Nudges are computed only while the founder is in the app. No scheduled worker sends anything, and the reminders table is not polled.

answers.question: Can a framework be applied to my business, or is it just something to read?
answers.answer:
It does not apply itself, but it is not only reading either.

Each framework has a space for your own notes, and that is where it becomes about your business — you work your actual problem through it and write down what came out. Those notes stay with the framework, so you can come back to them.

Ally will not fill a framework in for you. But you can bring one into the chat: say which framework and what you are deciding, and it will think it through with you using what it knows about your business.

That combination is where they earn their keep.
answers.verified_how: Framework notes are stored per founder and documented as never AI-written. Nothing auto-applies a framework to a founder's data.

answers.question: Does the calendar actually put tasks in my Google Calendar?
answers.answer:
Yes, if you have connected one. Tasks you set in Plan Your Day are added to your Google Calendar as real events, and edits follow.

That also makes it the most reliable way to be reminded, because your calendar can reach you when Ally is closed and Ally itself cannot.

You connect it from Plan Your Day. If you cannot see a Connect option, calendar syncing is not switched on for your account yet.

If you connected one and nothing is appearing, please tell support — that is a fault and we would want to see it.
answers.verified_how: A real push exists: creating or editing a task pushes an event and records the outcome. The Connect button is hidden entirely where the OAuth client is not configured.

That table was in Supabase, which is NOT the production database — production runs on AWS RDS. Confirmed by the team that calendar sync works on the real domain and that they have connected their own. The answer stands as written.

answers.question: Can I turn notifications off?
answers.answer:
Yes. Go to Profile, then Preferences, and switch Notifications off.

That stops the nudges Ally shows you inside the app — reminders about tasks, replies, and updates about your report.

It does not change anything outside the app, because there is nothing to change: Ally does not send reminder emails or phone notifications. The only email it sends is about discovery calls.

If you have connected a calendar, its reminders are separate and keep working. You would turn those off in your calendar, not here.
answers.verified_how: The Notifications switch controls in-app nudges. Only discovery-call notifications send email anywhere in the product.

answers.question: What is Know My Energy for?
answers.answer:
It is not built yet, and the page says so rather than pretending.

The idea is to look at how your energy actually moves through a week — when you do your sharpest work, when you are running on empty — and use that to plan around it instead of against it.

Today there is nothing to use. Opening it gives you an honest "coming soon".

Until then, Plan Your Day is where you shape your week, and Ally will talk through your working patterns with you if you ask it.
answers.verified_how: The page renders a deliberate 'Coming soon' panel. Nothing behind it exists.

answers.question: What happens on a discovery call, and who am I talking to?
answers.answer:
It is 30 minutes with someone from our team, not a bot.

You pick a time that suits you, and the team confirms it. Once they do, your call appears under "Your calls" on the Discovery call page with a Join button, and you also get an email with the time and the link.

The useful version of the call is you bringing something specific: your report, a decision you are stuck on, or a finding you disagree with. Say what you want to cover when you request it, and they will come prepared.

It is a conversation, not a presentation.

answers.note: Deliberately says the link is on the page FIRST and the email second. The page is the path that cannot silently fail; the email depends on EMAIL_HOST being configured.

answers.question: Is the discovery call free? Why can't I book one?
answers.answer:
It is not free. A discovery call costs Rs 300 for 30 minutes, on every plan.

That is per call. No plan includes one, so nobody has an allowance to run out of.

Asking for a slot costs nothing, though. You pick a time and send the request, our team checks it against their diary and confirms, and payment comes after that -- once you know the call is actually happening.

If the button is not there at all, it is because discovery calls are not included on the free plan.

answers.question: How many calls do I get, and what does an extra one cost?
answers.answer:
As many as you like, and each one costs Rs 300.

There is no limit and no allowance. Book one call or book six -- every one is Rs 300 for 30 minutes, and it is the same price on every plan.

So there is no such thing as an extra call here. There is just the next call, at the same price as the last one.

You are only charged once the team has confirmed the time. Requesting a slot costs nothing.

answers.question: Can I just talk to a person instead of doing all this?
answers.answer:
You can, and a discovery call is how.

It is worth knowing what you lose, though. Without the diagnosis, whoever you speak to is starting from scratch in 30 minutes, the same as any first meeting. With it, they already know how you work and what Ally found, and the call starts somewhere useful.

So if you have the time, do the diagnosis first and bring the report. If you do not, request a call anyway and say what is going on.

For anything shorter, message support and a person will reply.

answers.question: Is the call going to be a sales pitch?
answers.answer:
It is not meant to be, and if it turns into one we would want to know.

The point of the call is your situation — going through your report, a decision you are stuck on, or something you think Ally got wrong.

If paid help would genuinely suit what you describe, they may mention it. What should not happen is a call that becomes a pitch when you came with a problem.

If that is what you get, please tell us afterwards. It is the kind of thing we would want to correct rather than defend.

answers.question: How do I move or cancel a call I've booked?

You can do both yourself, from your call in the app.

Cancel it if you no longer need it, or reschedule it to a different time — you do not have to email anyone. If the call was already confirmed, rescheduling creates the new meeting and sends you a fresh link. If it was still waiting on the team, it simply moves to the new time and stays with them.

Please change it as early as you can. The slot goes back for someone else, and the team plans their week around what is booked.

answers.answer:

Your billing page shows what you are on now and exactly what changes.

Pro adds the rest — Vision, Recommendations, asking Ally about our wider knowledge, email updates, and priority when you request a call.

answers.question: Is there a plan for two founders, or a whole team?

That is not only a billing decision. The diagnosis is built around one founder -- how you think, how you decide, where you get stuck -- so a shared login would give you a report about neither of you.

answers.question: What is a credit?
answers.answer:
A credit is how we measure your conversations with Ally.

A typical message and its reply costs about two or three credits. A long question, a detailed answer, or one where Ally reads a file you attached will cost more.

Your plan comes with a number of credits each month, and they refresh with it. Your billing page shows how many you have left.

You do not have to manage them day to day. For most founders they simply last the month.
answers.verified_how: One credit is 1,000 tokens; a measured exchange is about 2,400 tokens.

answers.question: What's the difference between a credit and a token?
answers.answer:
A token is how AI systems measure text — very roughly, a word and a bit. A credit is our unit, and one credit is a thousand tokens.

You will mostly see credits, because they are a size worth thinking about. Tokens turn up in your daily allowance.

If you would rather not think about either: a message and reply is about two or three credits, and your billing page shows what is left.
answers.verified_how: TOKENS_PER_CREDIT is 1,000. Daily ceilings are expressed in tokens; plan allowances in credits.

answers.question: Why are you measuring me in tokens? I don't know what a token is.
answers.answer:
That is fair — most people have no reason to know.

The honest reason is that tokens are what the AI itself charges by, so it is the only measure that does not quietly misprice things. If we counted whole messages instead, a one-word question and a two-page one would cost the same, and one of those would be subsidising the other.

You should not have to care, though. Your billing page shows what is left without you doing any arithmetic, and a typical message costs two or three credits.
answers.verified_how: Metering is token-based end to end; credits are the presentation layer over it.

answers.question: Why did one message cost more than another?
answers.answer:
Because length is what costs, not the number of messages.

A short question with a short answer costs little. A long question, a reply that goes into detail, or one where Ally had to read a document you attached all cost more.

Attaching a file is the biggest single jump. Ally has to read it before it can answer, and that reading is part of the cost.

So if you are making an allowance last, shorter and more specific questions go a good deal further.
answers.verified_how: Both the message and the reply are metered, and extracted attachment text is added to the prompt before the model sees it.

answers.question: Where do I see how much I have left?
answers.answer:
Go to Profile and look at Subscription and billing.

It shows your plan, how much of today's allowance you have used, and how many diagnoses you have used.

Two different things are worth telling apart there. Your daily allowance starts again each day. Your monthly credits refresh when your plan does.
answers.verified_how: The panel renders 'Talk to Ally — n / limit today' and 'AI Business Diagnosis — n / 1 lifetime'.

answers.question: Where do I see what I've used this month?
answers.answer:
The same place — Profile, then Subscription and billing.

It shows today's usage against your daily allowance, and where you are against your plan's credits.

What it does not show is a message-by-message breakdown. If a large amount went somewhere and you want to know where, ask support and we can look it up for you.
answers.verified_how: Usage is stored per day and per source. No per-message statement is exposed to founders.

answers.question: I still have credits but it says I've hit my limit. Which is it?
answers.answer:
Both are true. They are two different limits and you can meet either one first.

Your daily allowance caps how much you can use in a single day. Your credits are the monthly total.

If you hit the daily one, your credits are untouched and still waiting — you carry on tomorrow.

If you hit the credit one, the month's allowance is spent.

We know having two is confusing. Your billing page shows both, so you can see which one stopped you.
answers.verified_how: The daily ceiling and the credit balance are separate gates producing different refusals.

answers.question: When does the daily limit reset, and in which timezone?
answers.answer:
At midnight, India time.

It used to roll over at midnight UTC, which meant founders here got their allowance back at half past five in the morning. Someone who ran out at nine in the evening was told to wait for midnight, and then found nothing there until dawn. That is fixed.

There is no job to wait for either. The moment the date changes, the new day's allowance is simply there.
answers.verified_how: USAGE_RESET_TIMEZONE is Asia/Kolkata. Usage is keyed by local date rather than reset by a scheduled job, so a new day is a new counter.

answers.question: Do my credits expire?
answers.answer:
The ones that come with your plan do. They are for that month and do not stack up.

Any credits we have added to your account by hand — to make up for a problem, say — do not expire. Those stay until you use them.

When you spend, the expiring ones go first. That is deliberate: the credits with a deadline get used before the ones without, so you do not lose an allowance while sitting on a gift.
answers.verified_how: Two buckets: plan credits expire at renewal, granted credits do not. Deductions drain the monthly bucket first.

answers.question: I'm on Free — do I get credits again next month?

answers.question: Do unused messages carry over?
answers.answer:

Your daily allowance works the same way — it does not build up if you skip a day.

So there is no benefit to saving them. If there is something you have been meaning to ask Ally, asking is free in the sense that holding back does not buy you anything later.

answers.question: I've run out of messages. What now?
answers.answer:
It depends which limit you reached, and your billing page shows which.

If it was the daily one, nothing is lost. You carry on tomorrow with a full day's allowance.

If it was your monthly credits, the options are to wait for your renewal or move to a plan with a larger allowance.

One thing that is never affected: your report, your Founder DNA and everything already in your account stay exactly where they are. Running out stops new conversations, not access to what you have.
answers.verified_how: Both refusals block new chat only. Nothing already stored becomes unreachable.

answers.question: Can I buy more without subscribing?
answers.answer:
Not at the moment, sorry. There is no way to buy a one-off top-up of credits on its own.

If you need more, the way to get it today is a plan with a larger monthly allowance. Your billing page shows what each one includes.

A top-up is something we have considered rather than something we offer. If it is what you actually want, please tell us — knowing that people are asking is what moves it up the list.
answers.verified_how: A top-up price and credit amount exist as constants but there is no purchase path anywhere in the product, and checkout is not built.

answers.question: Does the diagnosis eat into my allowance?
answers.answer:
No, not at all. The diagnosis is not metered.

That is deliberate. Nobody should hit a wall halfway through answering questions about their own business, so it is limited by count instead — one per account — rather than by how much you use.

Answer at whatever length you like. Longer, more honest answers make the report better and cost you nothing.
answers.verified_how: The diagnosis is deliberately absent from the metered sources and bounded by a lifetime count instead.

answers.question: Does generating the report cost me anything?
answers.answer:
No. The report comes with the diagnosis, and neither is metered.

Downloading it as a PDF, sharing it, and coming back to read it again months later are all free too.

The only thing that uses your allowance is talking to Ally in chat.
answers.verified_how: Report generation, PDF export and share links are outside the metered path entirely.

answers.question: Does uploading a file cost credits?
answers.answer:
Yes. Ally has to read the file before it can answer, and that reading comes out of your chat allowance.

A long document costs more than a short one.

If you are watching your allowance, it helps to say which part matters. "Look at the pricing section" is cheaper than attaching forty pages and asking what Ally thinks — and it usually gets you a better answer as well.
answers.verified_how: Extracted attachment text is added to the prompt and metered with the message. The billing panel states this explicitly.

answers.question: Chat has run out. Can I still plan my day?
answers.answer:
Yes. Planning is not affected by your chat allowance at all.

Adding tasks, setting times, ticking things off and looking at your goals do not use it, because none of them need Ally to think about anything.

So even with chat completely used up for the day, your plan still works normally. That is on purpose — running out of one part of Ally should never take the rest down with it.
answers.verified_how: Chat and planning meter separately by source. Planning's counter reads zero because adding a task is deterministic and makes no model call.

answers.question: Does Plan Your Day have its own limit?
answers.answer:
In practice, no. Planning does not use up anything today.

There is a separate budget set aside for it, kept apart from chat so that running out of one can never disable the other. Nothing currently draws on it, because adding and completing tasks does not need Ally to think.

So plan as much as you like. The only thing your allowance limits is talking to Ally.
answers.verified_how: planning has its own metered source; the counter is zero in practice. The budget exists so reminder or notification model work has somewhere to land later without a schema change.

answers.question: Roughly how many messages a day does my plan give me?
answers.answer:
It depends on your plan and on how long your messages are, so the real answer is on your billing page rather than here.

As a rough guide, a typical message and reply costs two or three credits. Long questions, detailed answers and attached documents cost more.

Your billing page shows today's usage against your allowance, so after a day or two of normal use you will have a much better sense of it than any number we could print.
answers.verified_how: Deliberately no per-plan figure: daily ceilings differ by tier and are changing with the new pricing.

answers.question: Can I see what a message will cost before I send it?
answers.answer:
No, and it is a fair thing to want.

The cost depends on how long your message is and how long Ally's reply turns out to be, and the reply does not exist until it has been written. So there is nothing honest we could show you beforehand.

What you can do is watch the running total on your billing page, which updates as you go.

If a rough "this will cost about this much" would genuinely help you, tell us.
answers.verified_how: Metering happens after the model replies, since output tokens are part of the cost. No pre-flight estimate exists.

answers.question: If I downgrade, what happens to my report and my data?
answers.answer:
Nothing is deleted. Ever, for this reason.

Your report, your Founder DNA, your goals, your tasks and your past conversations all stay exactly where they are. Moving to a smaller plan changes what you can do next -- it never takes away what you already have.

What does change is access to some features. If you move down from Plus to Starter, for example, you keep your report but you stop being able to chat with Ally.

Move back up later and everything is where you left it.
answers.verified_how: Consistent with how the product already behaves: plan features gate new actions, and nothing in the codebase deletes founder data on a plan change. Verified there is no downgrade cleanup path anywhere.

answers.question: How do I change my profile photo?
answers.answer:
Go to Profile and click your picture, then choose a new one.

It accepts PNG, JPEG and WEBP, up to 5MB. The new photo replaces the old one straight away -- there is nothing to save.

One thing that catches people out: iPhones save photos as HEIC by default, and that is not accepted yet. If your photo will not upload, that is almost always why. Open it and export it as JPEG, or change Settings, then Camera, then Formats to "Most Compatible" so new photos are saved as JPEG.

If it still will not go, tell us what kind of file it is.
answers.verified_how: Live test: PNG upload returned 201 with a stored avatar URL; a GIF was refused with a clear message naming the accepted types. One photo per founder -- a new upload replaces the old.
answers.note: Same HEIC gap recorded against question 219. The picker's accept list means iPhone photos are greyed out in the file chooser with no error to read.

answers.question: Can I change the email on my account?
answers.answer:
Not yourself, but we can do it. Write to info@goxl.in.

Tell us the address you have now and the one you want, and send it from an address we can recognise.

We do it by hand on purpose. Your email is what proves the account is yours, so it is not something a form should change quietly.

If you have only just signed up and have not done anything yet, the simpler route is to sign up again with the right address and tell us to remove the first one.
answers.verified_how: Live-checked: /settings/account accepts preferred_language and nothing else, and the schema states plainly that email and plan are owned by auth and billing rather than editable here.
answers.finding: There is no in-product way to even ASK for this. A founder who mistyped their address at signup is signed in as an address they do not own and cannot reach us from inside the account. Worth an 'email change' action in the Privacy Center beside the correction request that already exists.

answers.question: I can't log in. I've forgotten my password.
answers.answer:
You do not need it. Ask for a code instead.

On the sign-in screen, choose the option to sign in with a code, type your email address and we send you an 8-digit code. Enter it and you can set a new password there and then.

The code takes a moment to arrive and it is often in spam. If nothing comes, wait 60 seconds and press Resend.

If your email address is the problem -- you cannot get into that inbox any more -- write to info@goxl.in and we will help.
answers.verified_how: Walked the sign-in flow: the email-and-code path is both the first sign-in and the forgotten-password route, and it ends by setting a new password. Codes are 8 digits and Resend unlocks after 60 seconds.

answers.question: Can I use the same account on my phone and my laptop?
answers.answer:
Yes. Sign in on both and use whichever suits you.

Everything is stored on our side, not on the device, so your report, your goals and your conversations are the same wherever you open them. Something you write on your phone is there on your laptop.

Signing in on one does not sign you out of the other.

The only thing worth knowing is that long documents -- your report especially -- are easier to read on a bigger screen.
answers.verified_how: Sessions are per browser: each device gets its own refresh token and signing in on one does not disturb another. All state is server-side.

answers.question: I share a laptop. How do I sign out everywhere?
answers.answer:
There is no button for that yet, and I would rather tell you than let you look for one.

Signing out only signs out the device you are on.

So on a shared laptop, the thing that matters is signing out on that laptop when you finish -- use Sign out in Profile rather than just closing the tab. That does end the session on that machine properly.

If you think someone else has been in your account, write to info@goxl.in and say so. We will help you secure it, and we would want to know.

We are looking at adding a proper "sign out everywhere".
answers.verified_how: Confirmed in code: /auth/logout revokes only the single refresh token presented, and revoked_tokens is keyed by jti with no founder_id column -- so no query exists that could end every session for one founder.
answers.finding: Cannot be built without a schema change, and it is the security control founders actually ask for. Needs a founder_id on revoked_tokens or a per-founder token generation counter. This is the control worth having instead of the session_timeout_minutes setting removed on 2026-09-05 -- it closes a real hole rather than a decorative one.

answers.question: I run two businesses. Can I have both on one account?
answers.answer:
No, one account is one business.

Running two means two accounts with two email addresses, and paying for each.

That is deliberate rather than a limitation we have not got to. Everything Ally builds -- your stage, your report, your goals -- is about one business. Two businesses in one account would give you a blurred read of both.

If you do run both accounts, use whichever fits the business you are working on that day. They stay completely separate.
answers.verified_how: Team decision 2026-09-06: multi-business accounts are not available. Confirmed in the product: one profile, one diagnosis, one report per account.
answers.note: Team decision, 2026-09-06.

answers.question: Can I give my cofounder access?
answers.answer:
No, there is no way to add a second person to your account.

No invite, no extra seat, no shared login. And please do not share your password -- everything in your account is tied to that one sign-in, including your billing.

If your cofounder wants their own read, they can sign up separately. Their diagnosis would be about them, which is the point -- Ally is looking at the founder as much as the business, and the two of you will not answer the same way.

Comparing the two reports is usually more useful than sharing one.
answers.verified_how: Team decision 2026-09-06: cofounder access is not available. Confirmed in the product: no second seat, no invite mechanism and no shared account exist.
answers.note: Team decision, 2026-09-06.

answers.question: Is there a mobile app?
answers.answer:
No app yet, but Ally works in your phone's browser.

Just open the site on your phone and sign in as usual. The menu moves to a button in the top left, and the pages fit the smaller screen.

Long things like your report are easier to read on a laptop, so if you have one, use it for the report and your phone for quick check-ins.

We do not have an app in the app stores yet.
answers.verified_how: Tested at 375x812: the main pages render with no horizontal overflow and the sidebar collapses to a menu button. There is no PWA manifest and no app store presence.

answers.question: Which browsers does this work on?
answers.answer:
Chrome, Edge, Firefox and Safari, as long as they are reasonably up to date.

Anything from the last two or three years is fine, on a computer or a phone. Internet Explorer is not supported at all.

If a page looks broken or will not load, the two things worth trying are updating your browser and doing a hard refresh, which clears the old copy your browser is holding.

If it still misbehaves, tell us which browser and version you are on. That is usually enough for us to find it.
answers.verified_how: React 19 on Vite 8, built for baseline-widely-available browsers. No legacy build and no polyfill bundle ships, so genuinely old browsers will not run the app at all.

answers.question: Can you read my conversations?
answers.answer:
Yes, a small number of people at GoXL can, and we would rather say that plainly than let you assume otherwise.

It is limited, and it is for support. If you write in saying Ally gave you a strange answer, somebody has to be able to look at what actually happened.

They can read. They cannot edit — there is no way for anyone here to change what you or Ally said, because that was never built.

Your conversations are not shared outside GoXL, not sold, and never shown to other founders.
answers.verified_how: Support and above hold VIEW_CHATS. The admin service has no write counterpart anywhere — deliberately, so 'view but never edit' is guaranteed by absence rather than by a guard.

answers.question: Who else sees my diagnosis?
answers.answer:
Nobody outside GoXL.

Inside GoXL, a small number of people can open it for support reasons — the same people who can look at a conversation if you report a problem.

It is not shared with other founders, not sold, and not shown to investors or partners. There is no directory, no ranking, and no way for another founder to find you.

If you do want somebody to see it, that is your call: your report has a Share button that creates a link, and you decide who gets it.
answers.verified_how: Reports are readable by admins holding VIEW_REPORTS. No cross-founder visibility exists anywhere in the product. Sharing is founder-initiated and revocable.

answers.question: Is my data used to train anything?
answers.answer:
Your own writing, never. Anonymous combined data, yes.

Here is the line, because it matters. Your answers, your report and your conversations are not used to train any AI model. They are not put into any searchable index either. They are stored as your records and read back for you, and nothing else.

What we may use is anonymous, combined information -- patterns across many founders, with nothing in them that could be traced back to you or your business. That is how Ally gets better at reading the next founder.

Our Terms and Privacy Policy both say this in full, and they are the authority if you want the exact wording.
answers.verified_how: Settled by the team on 2026-09-05: the position is what the Terms and Privacy Policy already say. Terms section 4, Privacy Policy sections 3(c) and 6 all permit anonymised aggregated use to improve GoXL's AI models. The first half is separately verified in code -- the eight embedded tables are all GoXL reference knowledge, and no founder-owned table carries an embedding column, so founder text is never vectorised or trained on.
answers.note: Team decision, 2026-09-05. Earlier drafts of this answer said flatly that nothing is used to train any model, which contradicted three clauses in our own published documents. The team's call was to follow the documents. The distinction the answer draws -- your writing never, anonymous aggregate yes -- is exactly the distinction the Terms draw, and it is the honest one.

answers.question: How do I delete everything?
answers.answer:
Go to Profile, then Privacy Center, then "Delete my account".

That schedules erasure with a 30-day window. Until that date your account works normally and nothing has been removed, so a mis-click is recoverable.

If you change your mind, just sign in again before the date and we will offer you the chance to cancel it.

If you want a copy of your data before it goes, use "Download my data" on the same page first. After the date, it cannot be recovered.
answers.verified_how: Deletion is scheduled with a 30-day grace window. Signing in during it shows a blocking prompt offering a one-click cancel.

answers.question: Where is my data stored? Is it in India?
answers.answer:
Yes. Your data is stored in India — our servers and database run in the Mumbai region.

That is a deliberate choice for a product built for Indian founders: your business information stays in the country rather than being moved somewhere else for convenience.

If you need the specifics for a compliance or diligence question, write to support and we will give you a proper answer rather than a summary.
answers.verified_how: The application load balancer and the Supabase project are both in ap-south-1 (Mumbai).
answers.finding: CONFIRM BEFORE PUBLISHING. Production runs on AWS RDS, and its region has not been verified from here — only the load balancer and the Supabase project were. A data residency claim is one of the few things worth being certain about. See docs/PRODUCTION-RDS-CHECKS.md.

answers.question: Does what I type go to an outside AI company?
answers.answer:
Yes, in a limited and anonymous way, and our privacy policy says so.

Ally uses outside AI services to do some of its thinking. What goes to them is anonymised first, and they are bound by data handling agreements that stop them keeping it or using it for their own purposes.

What does not happen: your name, your business name and your account are not part of what is sent, and nothing you write is used to train anyone's model.

We do not name which services we use. That is a commercial decision and it can change.

If you need the specifics for a compliance review, write to us and we will answer properly.
answers.verified_how: Privacy Policy section 5(b), verbatim: 'AI Processing Services -- anonymised diagnostic data may be processed by third-party LLM providers under strict data handling agreements.' That discloses the category without naming a vendor, which is exactly what the never-name-the-model rule needs.
answers.note: Was open_for_team. Unblocked by reading the published Privacy Policy, which had already answered it at the right level of detail -- the collision with 'never name the model' was only ever a collision if we tried to answer it more specifically than the policy does.

answers.question: Can someone at GoXL open my account and read it?
answers.answer:
Yes, and we would rather you knew than found out.

A small number of people here can open your account to help with a problem — your profile, your report, your conversations. It is limited to the people who answer founders.

They can look. They cannot change anything you or Ally wrote; that was never built.

Anything they do change — resetting something, correcting a record — is written to a log with who did it and when.

Nobody outside GoXL has this access, and none of it is shared or sold.
answers.verified_how: Read capabilities are VIEW_USERS, VIEW_REPORTS and VIEW_CHATS. Every mutation records an audit entry with admin, founder, action and IP. No edit path exists for founder or Ally messages.

answers.question: What does "pause AI processing" do, and what stops working if I use it?
answers.answer:
It stops Ally thinking about you, and nothing else.

While it is on you cannot send messages to Ally or start a diagnosis. Both stop with a notice telling you to resume from the Privacy Center.

Everything you already have stays exactly as it is. Your account is active, your report is readable, and nothing is deleted.

You can turn it back on whenever you like — there is a Resume button in the amber banner at the top of Profile, then Privacy Center, and it takes effect straight away.
answers.verified_how: Tested live: with processing restricted, a chat message returns a clear refusal naming the Privacy Center. Nothing stored is affected, and resuming restores normal function immediately.

answers.question: What's actually in the data export? Can I read it?
answers.answer:
Everything we hold about you, as a file that downloads straight away.

It covers 23 areas: your profile and settings, your diagnosis sessions and answers, your Founder DNA answers, your reports, your conversations and messages, your goals and tasks, calls you booked, feedback you sent, and the record of privacy requests like this one.

It is a JSON file. That is readable rather than pretty — open it in a browser or any text editor and you will find your way around.

If you need it in a different form, ask support.
answers.verified_how: Ran the export: 23 named sections, served immediately as JSON.

answers.question: If I delete my account, is it gone immediately?
answers.answer:
No, and that is on purpose.

Deletion is scheduled with a 30-day window. Until that date your account works normally and nothing has been removed — so if you clicked it by mistake, or simply changed your mind, you have time.

Sign in again before the date and we will offer to cancel it. You do not have to email anybody.

After the date it is permanent and cannot be undone, so take a copy of anything you want to keep before then.
answers.verified_how: 30-day grace window with a self-serve cancel offered on next sign-in.

answers.question: Can I use Ally without giving my real business name?
answers.answer:
Yes. Your business name is optional and nothing is blocked without it.

Ally works from what you describe — your stage, who you serve, what is stuck — rather than from who you are. Leave the name out or keep it vague and the diagnosis is unaffected.

What does matter is being honest about the situation itself. A made-up business name costs you nothing. A made-up answer about your revenue costs you the accuracy of the report.
answers.verified_how: business_name is an optional column and nothing in the profile or diagnosis path requires it.

answers.question: Could anything I say here ever be shown to an investor or a partner?
answers.answer:
Not by us. Never.

We do not share your data with investors, partners or anyone else outside GoXL, and we do not sell it.

The only way anything of yours reaches someone else is if you send it. Your report has a Share button that creates a link, and you decide who gets it.

If you would rather nothing was shareable at all, simply do not create one.
answers.verified_how: The only outbound path for founder content is a founder-created share link, which is revocable and expires after 30 days.

answers.question: If I stop using it, do you keep my data forever?
answers.answer:
We keep it until you ask us to delete it. There is no automatic clear-out after a stretch of not using Ally.

That is deliberate: you can come back in a year and your report is still there, rather than having quietly disappeared while you were busy.

If you would rather it did not sit there, you can delete your account whenever you like from Profile, then Privacy Center — with the same 30-day window before it becomes permanent.
answers.verified_how: No inactivity-based retention or purge job exists anywhere. The only deletion path is founder-initiated.

answers.question: I uploaded a file and Ally says it can't see it.
answers.answer:
Ally can read documents. It cannot read pictures.

PDFs, Word files, plain text and CSV all work. Ally reads what is inside them and can quote your own numbers back to you.

Images are different. A PNG, a JPEG or a screenshot will upload, but Ally cannot see what is in it. The same is true of a photo or a scan of a document.

If your file is a picture, the quickest fix is to type the important part into the chat, or upload the original document instead of a photo of it.
answers.verified_how: Uploaded a CSV and Ally quoted the exact figures back. Uploaded a PNG and it correctly said it could not read the contents -- it no longer claims to have looked at it.
answers.note: Ally used to claim it had read images it could never see. The prompt said 'attached for you to look at' while the transport carried text only. Fixed on 2026-09-04 by setting the media limit to zero, so the model is never told an image is there.

answers.question: My calendar won't connect.
answers.answer:
Go to Plan Your Day and press Connect calendar. Google asks you to sign in and allow access. When you come back, the page tells you what happened.

If it did not work, the message on that page says why. The three common ones:

"Link expired" means you took too long on the Google screen. Press Connect again.

"Google refused the connection" often means you signed in with a different Google account. Use the one your calendar is on.

If you pressed Cancel on the Google screen, nothing was saved. Just start again.

If it keeps failing, write to us and tell us which message you saw.
answers.verified_how: Read the callback: it always redirects back to Plan Your Day carrying one of four outcomes, each with a readable sentence. Calendar sync is confirmed working on production by the founder who owns that account.

answers.question: My profile photo won't upload.
answers.answer:
Ally accepts PNG, JPEG and WEBP, up to 5MB.

The most common reason it fails is an iPhone photo. iPhones save pictures as HEIC by default, and that is not accepted yet. GIFs are not accepted either.

The fix is to open the photo and save or export it as JPEG, then upload that.

On an iPhone you can also change Settings, then Camera, then Formats to "Most Compatible", so new photos are saved as JPEG from then on.

If the file is very large, make it smaller first.
answers.verified_how: Live test: PNG returned 201 with a stored avatar URL. A GIF was refused with a clear message naming the accepted types. HEIC is neither accepted server-side nor offered in the picker.
answers.finding: On an iPhone the founder's own photos are greyed out in the file chooser, so there is no error to read and nothing to explain the failure. Accept HEIC and convert, or add one line of help text beside the button.

answers.question: The page is stuck on "thinking".
answers.answer:
That screen is waiting for your report to be built. It usually takes under a minute.

If it is taking longer, the screen says so and tells you that you can close it. That is true. Your answers are all saved, and leaving the page loses nothing.

Come back to Report from the menu a few minutes later and it will be there.

If it is still not there an hour later, write to us and tell us roughly when you finished. We will find it.
answers.verified_how: The screen polls for the report every 4 seconds and switches its own copy to 'This is taking longer than usual. Your answers are saved.' after about two minutes. It never spins silently.

answers.question: I found a bug. Where do I report it?
answers.answer:
Go to Help & Support and press "Report a bug". That opens the Feedback page with the right topic already chosen, so you only have to describe what happened.

The most useful thing you can tell us is what you were doing just before it broke, and what you saw on screen. A screenshot helps more than anything.

It comes straight to our team. It is not a form that goes nowhere.
answers.verified_how: The Help & Support quick action carries the topic through to the Feedback page, and the note posts to the backend and lands in founder_feedback.

answers.question: My report page is blank.
answers.answer:
There are two different things this can be.

If you have not finished a diagnosis yet, the page says "Your report isn't ready yet" and offers a button to start one. That is the normal state, not a fault.

If you have done the diagnosis and the page is empty, it is almost always still loading. Give it a moment, then refresh the page.

If a refresh does not fix it, write to us. Your report is stored on our side, so a blank page never means it has been lost.
answers.verified_how: Opened /app/report on an account with no diagnosis: a proper empty state with a Start Founder Diagnosis button. The only genuinely blank moment is the second or two while it loads.

answers.question: It signed me out in the middle of the diagnosis.
answers.answer:
Sign back in and carry on. You will not have to start again.

Every answer is saved the moment you send it, so the diagnosis picks up from the question you were on.

It also does not count as a used diagnosis. Only a finished one counts, so nothing has been spent.

Being signed out part way through is unusual. It normally means you signed out somewhere else, or your browser cleared its stored data. If it keeps happening, tell us which browser you use and we will look.
answers.verified_how: Answers are persisted one at a time on submit, and the submit path is idempotent when resumed. Sessions renew automatically for 30 days, so a mid-session sign-out is genuinely rare.

answers.question: It says I've hit a limit and I've only just started.
answers.answer:
The daily allowance is not counted in messages. It is counted in words, roughly speaking, and a long message costs a lot more than a short one.

Ally also reads your report and your profile before it replies, so even a short question is not free.

That is why a handful of long messages can use up a day, and it is not a fault.

The message you saw says which limit you reached, and your billing page shows today's usage against your allowance.

If that page shows you have barely used anything and you are still blocked, that is a fault. Write to us.
answers.verified_how: Measured the real cost from the database: 54 messages, average 1,305 tokens, largest 2,776. The daily error names the exact numbers and the reset time, so a founder can check it against the billing page.
answers.finding: On Plus (Rs 450, 3,500 tokens a day) that average works out at two or three messages. This complaint will be literally true for a founder who has just paid, on their first sitting. The ceiling needs raising -- no support answer covers it.

answers.question: Everything is very slow.
answers.answer:
Two things are usually behind it.

The first is the Compass page. It gathers a lot at once and is the slowest page in Ally, especially the first time you open it after signing in. We know, and we are working on it.

The second is simply a slow connection. Ally sends a fair amount back and forth.

If one particular page is slow every single time, tell us which one and roughly how long it takes. That is far more useful to us than "it is slow", and it gets fixed faster.
answers.verified_how: Compass took several seconds to fill in on a warm local build with no other load. Traced earlier to database pool contention when its panels all load together.

answers.question: It looks broken on my phone.
answers.answer:
Ally works in a phone browser. We checked the main pages at phone size and they fit, with nothing running off the side of the screen.

There is no app to install yet. Use Chrome or Safari.

If a page looks wrong, it is usually an old copy stored by your browser after we released an update. Pull down to refresh, or close the tab and open it again.

If it still looks wrong, send us a screenshot and tell us which phone you have. That is the only way we can see what you are seeing.
answers.verified_how: Tested at 375x812: /app, /app/report and /app/ally-chat all render with zero horizontal overflow and the sidebar collapses to a menu button.

answers.question: Where does my feedback actually go? Does anyone read it?
answers.answer:
It comes to our team, and yes, we read all of it.

Both things on the Feedback page, the written note and the star rating, are saved on our side and show up for the team straight away.

This used to be worse. The written note used to open your own email app, which quietly did nothing if you did not have one set up. That is fixed. It now reaches us directly.

We do not reply to every one. If you would like an answer, say so in the note.
answers.verified_how: Both the note and the rating POST to the same endpoint and land in the same founder_feedback table, which the team reads.

answers.question: If I message support, how long until someone replies?
answers.answer:
We aim to reply within one working day.

We are here Monday to Friday, 9 AM to 6 PM India time. A message sent on Saturday evening will be picked up on Monday.

You can reach us at info@goxl.in, or through Help & Support inside Ally, which sends your name and email along so you do not have to repeat them.

If it is urgent, say so at the top of your message. Money leaving your account, or not being able to get in, go to the front of the queue.
answers.verified_how: Read from the Help & Support page as it stands today: info@goxl.in, Mon-Fri 9 AM - 6 PM IST, 'We aim to reply within one working day.' Stated as an aim, with no invented average.

answers.question: Is Ally a coach, a consultant, or a tool?
answers.answer:
None of the three, and the difference matters.

A coach asks you questions. A consultant hands you answers. A tool waits for you to know what to do with it.

Ally is a compass. It works out where you actually are first -- you and the business -- and then points at the one thing to move next.

The way we put it is this: most AI gives you answers, Ally helps you find the right question. The problem you can see is often not the problem you need to solve.

So it is not there to advise you, or to be clever. It is there so you stop guessing which problem is the real one.
answers.verified_how: The settled position, matching the landing page word for word: 'Your Founder's Compass' and 'Most AI gives you answers. Ally helps you find the right question.'

answers.question: Can this replace a real mentor or advisor?
answers.answer:
No, and we would not want it to.

A good mentor gives you judgement, a network, and someone who has done it before and cares how it goes for you. Ally has none of that.

What Ally has is different. It is there at eleven at night. It has read every answer you gave it. It never gets tired of the same question, and it has no reason to tell you what you want to hear.

The useful way to use both is together. Bring your report to your mentor. It saves the first hour of every conversation.

If you want a person from our side, you can book a discovery call.
answers.verified_how: Consistent with answers 76 and 147: a discovery call is 30 minutes with a real person, and the report is what makes that conversation start somewhere useful.

answers.question: Is a human involved in any of what I get?
answers.answer:
In your report, no. It was written by AI, and no person read it before you did.

People built what it works from. The framework, the questions, the six areas and the way a root cause is found were all designed by our team. Ally cannot go outside that, and it is not allowed to invent findings.

There are two places a person is genuinely involved. A discovery call is 30 minutes with someone from our team. And when you message support, a person replies.

We would rather be plain about this than let you imagine somebody is reading over your shoulder.
answers.verified_how: Matches answer 44. The report is generated with no human review step anywhere in the pipeline. The prompt forbids inventing findings. Discovery calls and support are the two human surfaces.

answers.question: Who built this, and what qualifies them to diagnose my business?
answers.answer:
GoXL built it. Entrepreneurs, building for entrepreneurs.

But the honest answer to "what qualifies it" is not somebody's CV. It is what sits underneath.

Ally was built from real founder work: more than 10,000 founder case studies, and 25,000 founder problems traced back to what actually caused them, across more than a hundred areas.

And the root cause is not an AI's opinion. Your answers are scored against that framework, and the framework decides. The AI's job is to explain the result in plain language, not to reach it.

If you want to talk to the people behind it, book a discovery call.
answers.verified_how: Corpus figures are the landing page's own, verbatim, and match answers 34 and 60. 'For the entrepreneurs, by the entrepreneurs' is the landing page's phrase. The deterministic-engine point is true of the code: the engine picks the root cause and the model narrates it.
answers.finding: Nothing public names the team or their track record. If a founder pushes past this answer we have nothing to give them. A short 'about us' page the bot can point at would close it.

answers.question: Do you work with my competitors?
answers.answer:
Possibly. Anyone can sign up, and we do not offer exclusivity to anyone in any industry.

What matters is that it changes nothing for you. Nothing of yours is ever visible to another founder. There is no directory, no ranking, and no way for anyone to find you or to see your report.

You are not compared against named businesses either. Your report measures you against the framework, not against the founder down the road.

Your data is never sold, and never shared outside GoXL.
answers.verified_how: No exclusivity mechanism exists anywhere in the product, and no cross-founder visibility of any kind. Consistent with answers 38 and 205.

answers.question: Is this only for Indian founders?
answers.answer:
It is built for Indian founders, but it is not closed to anyone else.

Almost everything is set up around India. Prices are in rupees. Your data is stored in India. Support runs Monday to Friday, 9 AM to 6 PM India time.

Nothing in Ally checks where you are, so it works wherever you sit. The questions are about your stage and your business, not your country.

If you are outside India and thinking of paying, write to us first. We would rather sort that out with you than have you find a problem at checkout.
answers.verified_how: No geographic restriction exists in the code. Prices are in INR, support hours are IST, and residency is India. Deliberately does not promise foreign payment -- question 185 is still open.
answers.note: Kept vague on paying from outside India on purpose. Question 185 (foreign payment) is still with the team, and checkout is not built.

answers.question: Is my business too small -- or too big -- for this?
answers.answer:
Almost certainly not.

There are eight stages, from just exploring an idea all the way to exit. You do not need revenue, customers, a team, or even a registered company. If you only have an idea, Ideation is a real stage and the diagnosis is built for it.

At the other end, Ally is built around a founder-led business -- one person whose decisions still shape the company. If you have a full leadership team and your own decisions are no longer the constraint, less of it will apply.

Solo founders, small teams, family businesses and bootstrapped builders are all squarely who this is for.
answers.verified_how: founder_stages holds all eight stages from Ideation to Exit, and the diagnosis scopes itself to fewer pillars at the early ones rather than refusing them. The audience list is the landing page's own.

answers.question: What's coming next? Can I ask for a feature?
answers.answer:
Yes, please do. Go to Feedback and choose "I have an idea". It comes straight to our team, and we read all of it.

We do not publish a roadmap, mainly because we would rather not promise dates we then miss.

One thing we have committed to in writing: being able to run the diagnosis again when your business stage changes. That is intended, and not built yet.

If you tell us what you want and why, it genuinely counts. Several things in Ally are there because a founder asked.
answers.verified_how: The Feedback page's 'I have an idea' topic posts to founder_feedback, which the team reads. The re-run commitment is the only forward promise made anywhere in the answer set (answer 85), so it is the only one repeated here.

answers.question: What does Ally deliberately not do?
answers.answer:
A short and honest list.

It does not invent things about your business. It works only from what you told it and what the framework found.

It does not answer questions about the product itself -- your plan, your bill, your allowance. That is what Help & Support is for.

It does not produce files. It will help you write a pitch deck in the chat, but it cannot hand you a PowerPoint. Your report is the one document you can download.

It does not chase you. No emails, no nudges outside the app.

It does not rank you against other founders, and it never shows your work to anyone else.
answers.verified_how: Every item on this list is a real, checked behaviour: the no-invention rule is in the system prompt, the help-content boundary is answer 99, the no-file-export limit is answer 91, the no-outbound-nudge limit is answer 137, and no cross-founder visibility exists anywhere.
answers.finding: Legal, tax and investment advice was deliberately LEFT OFF this list. No such boundary exists in the product -- the prompt library, the knowledge base and the grounding prompts state nothing about what Ally may advise on. Question 100 is open for exactly this reason. Add it here only after the boundary is built, never before.

answers.question: The site says 100+ dimensions. My report covers six areas. Which is it?
answers.answer:
Both are true, and it is a fair thing to ask.

The six areas are how your findings are laid out so the report can be read: Founder Readiness, Market Clarity, Revenue Maturity, Product & Execution, Team & Leadership, and Strategic Clarity.

Underneath them sit more than a hundred smaller things Ally can look at. Founder DNA alone covers 15. Business DNA has its own set, and which ones apply depends on your stage.

So the six are the shelves, not the contents. If everything assessed was printed one by one, the report would be a spreadsheet, and you would not read it.
answers.verified_how: The '100+ entrepreneurial dimensions' claim is still on the live page and matches what the product does. Founder DNA's 15 dimensions are in the enum; the six pillars are the report's organising structure.

answers.question: Where is the founder health score the homepage promised me?
answers.answer:
Your Compass page has it. It is called Founder Clarity, and it is a word rather than a number.

Business health sits next to it, in the same style.

If yours is empty, there are two likely reasons. You may not have finished a diagnosis yet. Or you are at Ideation stage, where we deliberately do not publish a business health reading, because there is not yet enough business to measure honestly.

A made-up number would be worse than a blank. That gap is on purpose.
answers.verified_how: The live page no longer promises a health score, so the premise is retired -- but the Compass genuinely shows Founder Clarity as a band, and ideation-stage reports deliberately publish no business health figure. Consistent with answer 40.
answers.note: Premise gone from the current site. Kept and answered because founders who read the older page will still ask.

answers.question: The demo showed a diagnosis confidence figure. Where's mine?
answers.answer:
It is on your report, not in the chat.

Near the top you will see a line like "Ally's finding - High confidence". There are three levels: High, Moderate and Early.

If it says Early, your report also opens with a short note about certainty, explaining that Ally did not get quite enough to be sure.

We show it as a word on purpose. A number invites you to argue with the number instead of reading the finding.
answers.verified_how: The current sample dashboard shows no confidence readout at all, so the premise is retired. Confidence genuinely appears on the report as a band -- verified by opening a real report. Consistent with answers 47 and 48.

answers.question: It said three priority actions. I got a different number.
answers.answer:
Three is what the website shows as an example, not a promise.

Your report gives you what your diagnosis actually supports. For most founders that is two or three. It is never a long list.
