That is deliberate. A list of ten things to fix is the same as no list, because you will do none of them.

If you got fewer than you expected, it usually means Ally found one thing sitting underneath the rest, and would rather you did that one properly.
answers.verified_how: 'Three things to focus on first' is still on the live page, shown as an illustration alongside made-up examples. The real count comes from the diagnosis. Consistent with answer 129.

answers.question: What is the "Clarity Method"? Is it something you invented?
answers.answer:
That is not a name we use any more, so if you saw it, it was an older version of the site.

What sits behind Ally is our own framework, built deliberately rather than borrowed. Six areas, more than a hundred things underneath them, and a set of rules that traces what you told us back to the one cause sitting underneath.

It came out of real founder work: more than 10,000 founder case studies, and 25,000 founder problems traced back to what caused them.

So: made by us, but not made up.
answers.verified_how: The term 'Clarity Method' appears nowhere on the live site. The framework description matches answer 34 and the landing page's own corpus figures.

answers.question: The site calls it a Clarity Report. Inside it's just "report". Same thing?
answers.answer:
Same thing. One document, two names, and that is our untidiness rather than yours.

Inside Ally the page is called Report, and the browser tab still says "Clarity report". They are the same document, built from the same diagnosis.

There is only ever one report per account, so there is nothing to mix up. Whatever it is called, it is the one you are looking at.
answers.verified_how: Walked it: the app's own page title is literally 'Clarity report - Ally - GoXL' while the sidebar says Report. The term no longer appears on the live marketing site.

answers.question: Can I see a sample report before I sign up?
answers.answer:
No, and we have decided not to make one.

There is a sample of the app on our website, so you can look around and see how it is laid out. But there is no sample report, and there will not be.

The reason is that a report only means anything with a real founder's answers behind it. A made-up one would look impressive and tell you nothing about whether it would be useful to you -- and it would set an expectation your own report might not match, because yours is about your business, not a tidy invented one.

If you want a proper sense of it before deciding, ask support and we will talk you through what is in one.
answers.verified_how: Team decision 2026-09-05: no sample report will be produced. The site's embedded sample dashboard (/ally-dashboard.html) remains and is what the answer points at.
answers.note: Team decision, 2026-09-05.

answers.question: It says "no sales call". So what is the discovery call?
answers.answer:
The current site does not make that claim, so it may have been an older version.

Either way, here is the plain answer. A discovery call is 30 minutes with someone from our team, and it costs Rs 300. It is not included free on any plan.

It is not a pitch. There is nothing to upsell you to on the call, because the plans are on the website and you can read them yourself.

The useful version is you bringing something specific: your report, a decision you are stuck on, or a finding you disagree with.
answers.verified_how: The phrase 'no sales call' appears nowhere on the live site. Call price and shape match the team's decision of 2026-09-05: Rs 300 per 30-minute call, on every plan.
answers.note: Price set by the team on 2026-09-05. Raised from Rs 199 so it is not confused with the Rs 199 monthly Starter plan.

answers.question: It says private and encrypted. Encrypted how, and from whom?
answers.answer:
Encrypted on the way to us, and encrypted where it is stored.

Everything between you and Ally travels over an encrypted connection, so nobody in between can read it. Where it is stored, it is encrypted there too. Connected accounts like your calendar have their keys encrypted separately, and if that encryption is not available the feature switches itself off rather than storing anything in the clear.

Now the part the word "encrypted" can hide.

Encrypted from outsiders, yes. Not from us. A small number of people at GoXL can open your account to help with a support problem. They can read. They cannot edit.

It is never sold, and never shown to other founders.
answers.verified_how: Verified in the repo: all traffic is HTTPS, and calendar tokens are encrypted with a key whose absence disables the feature rather than falling back to plaintext. Encryption at rest confirmed by the team on 2026-09-06 -- it is in place, matching the Privacy Policy section 8 claim of AES-256. Staff read access (VIEW_CHATS, VIEW_REPORTS) is real and has no write counterpart anywhere.
answers.note: Team decision, 2026-09-06. The at-rest half was previously withheld because it could not be verified from the codebase while the Privacy Policy already claimed it publicly. The team has confirmed it is in place, so the answer now matches the policy.

answers.question: What should I have ready before I start?
answers.answer:
Nothing you have to look up. That is rather the point.

It helps to have a rough sense of three things: what stage you are at, roughly how much money is coming in and from how many customers, and what is actually stuck right now.

You do not need documents, exact figures, or anything to upload. Ally asks in plain language, and approximate answers are fine.

What does matter is being honest rather than tidy. A polished answer gets you a polished report about a business that does not exist.

Set aside about half an hour, somewhere you can think.
answers.verified_how: Walked the guided flow: nothing in onboarding or the diagnosis requires a document, an exact figure, or a registered company. Consistent with answers 13, 25 and 214.

answers.question: How long does the whole thing take, start to finish?
answers.answer:
About 30 to 40 minutes, and you can stop whenever you like.

Setting up your profile takes under five minutes. Founder DNA is up to 16 questions. The diagnosis itself is between 14 and 32 questions, depending on your stage -- early-stage founders get fewer, because there is less business to ask about.

Then the report is built for you. That usually takes under a minute.

Nothing has to be done in one sitting. Every answer is saved as you send it, so you can close the tab and come back.
answers.verified_how: Question budgets read from founder_stages: 14 at Ideation up to 32 at Expansion and Maturity. Founder DNA is capped at 16. The site's own 'under 5 minutes' onboarding and '20 to 30 minutes, resumable' diagnosis match this.

answers.question: Why is there no password? I don't want a code every time.
answers.answer:
You do have a password, and you will not need a code every time.

The code is only for two moments: the very first time you sign in, and if you forget your password later.

When you enter that code, you choose a password there and then. It needs to be at least 8 characters. After that, signing in is just your email and that password.

So if you are being asked for a code more than once, something has gone wrong. Tell us and we will look.
answers.verified_how: Read the sign-in flow: three steps on one screen. The email-and-code path is only for a first sign-in or a forgotten password; returning founders use email and password. Minimum password length is 8.

answers.question: My code hasn't arrived.
answers.answer:
Give it a minute, then try these in order.

Check your spam or junk folder. That is where it is most of the time.

Check the email address you typed. One wrong letter and the code has gone somewhere else.

Then press Resend. The button unlocks 60 seconds after the last one, so if it looks disabled, wait a moment.

The code is 8 digits. If what arrived is shorter, it is not from us.

If nothing comes after two tries, write to info@goxl.in from the address you are trying to use, and we will sort it out.
answers.verified_how: Resend cooldown is 60 seconds, matching the mail provider's own minimum interval so the button never unlocks while sending is still refused. This project issues 8-digit codes.

answers.question: The code expired before I could use it.
answers.answer:
That is fine. Just ask for a new one.

Go back to the sign-in screen, type your email again, and press the button to send a code. A fresh one arrives and the old one stops working.

Codes are deliberately short-lived. It is what stops an old email in your inbox being useful to anyone else later.

One thing worth knowing: always use the newest code. If you have two emails from us, the older code will not work, and it is easy to open the wrong one.
answers.verified_how: Requesting a new code invalidates the previous one. The on-screen copy tells the founder it expires in a few minutes, and this answer deliberately does not print a number the identity provider's settings could change.

answers.question: I signed up with the wrong email address.
answers.answer:
You cannot change it yourself, so please write to us and we will do it.

Send a message to info@goxl.in. Tell us the wrong address you used and the right one you want, and send it from an address we can recognise.

We do it by hand on purpose. The email is what proves an account is yours, so it is not something a form should change quietly.

If you have not done anything in the account yet, the simpler route is to sign up again with the correct address and tell us to remove the first one.
answers.verified_how: Live-checked: /settings/account accepts preferred_language and nothing else. The schema states plainly that email and plan are owned by auth and billing and are not editable by the founder.

answers.question: I got an email saying someone signed in. Was that me?
answers.answer:
Quite possibly yes, if it was a device you had not used before.

Ally now emails you when your account is opened from a new device. It tells you what the device was and when. If it was you, there is nothing to do.

If it was not you, change your password. Open Ally the way you normally do, by typing our address into your browser, and use "forgot password" on the sign-in screen.

Our email will never contain a link for that. So if the email you got asks you to click something, it is not from us. Please forward it to info@goxl.in.

You can turn these off in Profile.
answers.verified_how: Built and tested on 2026-09-05. Live test: first device learned silently, same device again no email, same device on a different address in the same network no email, genuinely new device flagged. The email carries no link on purpose, so 'our emails never ask you to click' stays true and remains a usable test for phishing.
answers.finding: This answer is only safe while it stays true. If sign-in notification emails are ever switched on, this answer becomes dangerous advice and must be rewritten the same day.
answers.note: REPLACES the previous answer, which said we never send sign-in emails and that any such email was phishing. That was true until today and would have become dangerous advice the moment this shipped.

answers.question: It keeps signing me out.
answers.answer:
This should be fixed now. If it is still happening to you, please tell us.

The cause was having Ally open in more than one tab. The tabs could trip over each other while renewing your session, and one of them would lose and sign you out. That is sorted.

Two other things can still end a session early. Your browser may be set to clear its data when you close it. And private or incognito windows forget everything on purpose.

Otherwise you stay signed in for 30 days on your own computer.
answers.verified_how: Fixed 2026-09-05 with a cross-tab lock in services/api.js, and verified with two real browser tabs reloading at the same moment with no access token: one took the lock and refreshed, the other waited and reused the result. Zero 401s, neither signed out. The same test produced a revoked-token 401 before the fix.

answers.question: Can I stay signed in on my own machine?
answers.answer:
Yes, and you already are.

On your own computer Ally keeps you signed in for 30 days without asking again. You do not have to tick anything.

Behind the scenes it renews itself quietly while you use it, which is why you can close the tab, come back tomorrow, and still be there.

Two things end it early: signing out, and a browser set to clear its data when it closes.

On a shared or public computer, please do sign out when you finish.
answers.verified_how: Access tokens last 30 minutes and are renewed automatically from an HttpOnly refresh cookie that lasts 30 days.

answers.question: Can I have it open in two tabs at once?
answers.answer:
Yes, that is fine now.

There used to be a fault where two tabs could trip over each other and sign you out of one of them. It is fixed.

Both tabs share the same session, so you stay signed in on both, and anything you save in one appears in the other when it next loads.

If you do get signed out with two tabs open, that is worth telling us about, because it should not happen any more.
answers.verified_how: Verified with two real tabs reloading simultaneously: one refreshed the session, the other picked up the shared token. Zero 401s, neither tab signed out.

answers.question: What does the notifications toggle actually control?
answers.answer:
There is no notifications switch on your Profile any more. We took it out.

It did not do anything. There are no in-app notifications for it to turn off, so whichever way you set it, Ally behaved the same. Rather than leave a switch that does nothing, we removed it.

What does reach you has not changed. Ally shows anything overdue when you open it, and if you have connected a calendar, your tasks are on there with proper reminders.

When there is something real to switch off, the switch will come back.
answers.verified_how: Hidden on 2026-09-05 and verified live: the Preferences card now shows two switches, Call reminders by email and Reduced motion, both of which genuinely work.
answers.note: Team decision, 2026-09-05.

answers.question: What is "private mode", and what happens to my data if I leave it off?
answers.answer:
There is no private mode any more. We removed it, because it did nothing.

The switch claimed to keep your business data anonymised in aggregate insights. Nothing read it, so turning it on or off changed absolutely nothing about how your data was handled. A privacy control that does not control anything is worse than not having one, so it is gone.

What is actually true: your own answers, report and conversations are never used to train anything and are never in any searchable index. We may use anonymous, combined information -- patterns across many founders, with nothing traceable to you -- to improve Ally.

That applies to everybody. It was never something the switch changed.
answers.verified_how: Removed from the Profile page and the settings schema on 2026-09-05 and verified live -- the page now shows two switches and the words 'private mode' and 'aggregate insights' appear nowhere on it. The data position is the team's settled one, matching Terms section 4 and Privacy Policy sections 3(c) and 6.
answers.note: REWRITTEN after the team settled the aggregate-data question on 2026-09-05. An earlier draft said the data 'was never going into anything of the kind', which was true of the switch but not of the Terms. The honest version separates the two: the switch was empty, and the aggregate use is real but anonymous.

answers.question: What are these "aggregate insights" my business is going into?
answers.answer:
It means patterns, not your business.

Our Terms allow us to use anonymous, combined information to improve Ally -- things like which kinds of problem tend to sit underneath which symptoms, across many founders at once. Nothing in it can be traced back to you, your company or anything you wrote.

Your own material is never part of that. Your answers, your report and your conversations are not used to train anything, and are not in any searchable index.

The switch that used to mention this has been removed, because it did not actually control anything. The full wording is in our Terms and Privacy Policy.
answers.verified_how: Team's settled position, 2026-09-05: the Terms and Privacy Policy are the authority. Terms section 4, Privacy Policy sections 3(c) and 6. Separately verified in code that no founder-owned table carries an embedding column, so founder text is never vectorised.
answers.note: REWRITTEN. An earlier draft said aggregate insights did not exist, which was true of the product but contradicted our own Terms. The team's call was that the Terms are right.

answers.question: Can I choose what time Ally reminds me?
answers.answer:
No, there is no reminder time to set. Ally does not send timed reminders at all.

What you can control is your calendar. Connect it from Plan Your Day and your tasks go in with a reminder half an hour before, which you can then move around in your own calendar however you like.

A task with a date but no time is put at 9 in the morning, so the reminder lands early in the day rather than late the night before.

If you would like Ally itself to remind you at a time you choose, tell us. We are keeping a list.
answers.verified_how: The reminder settings were removed from the product on 2026-09-05 (team decision) -- they persisted and nothing read them. The 9am default described here is the calendar sync's own default hour, which is real and working.
answers.note: Team decision, 2026-09-05. Was 'not yet'; now it is a plain no.

answers.question: Can I keep goal reminders but turn task reminders off?
answers.answer:
No. Goals and tasks do not send reminders, so there is nothing to separate.

The only reminder switch in Ally is on your Profile -- "Call reminders by email" -- and it covers reminders before a discovery call you have booked.

What goals and tasks do instead is show up when you open Ally, and go into your calendar if you have connected one. If you want those quieter, your calendar is the place to change it.

If separate reminders would be useful, tell us which ones you would actually want.
answers.verified_how: The separate task_reminders and goal_reminders flags were removed on 2026-09-05 (team decision) -- neither was read by anything and neither was reachable in the UI. The email switch on Profile is now the only reminder control that exists.
answers.note: Team decision, 2026-09-05.

answers.question: Will Ally email me, or only notify me inside the app?
answers.answer:
Almost everything happens inside the app. We send very little email.

There are two. When you book a discovery call, you get an email confirming the time with the joining link. And if your account is opened from a device you have not used before, we let you know.

That is all. No daily emails, no weekly summaries, no marketing.

If you have connected a calendar, your task reminders come from your calendar rather than from us.
answers.verified_how: The only two founder-facing emails in the product are the discovery call booking confirmation and, as of 2026-09-05, the new-device sign-in notice. Call reminders exist and are now schedulable, and no marketing email exists anywhere.

answers.question: How do I stop all email from you?
answers.answer:
There is very little to stop, but here is what there is.

Go to Profile, then Preferences, and turn off "Call reminders by email". That covers reminders before a discovery call.

Two we would rather you kept. The confirmation when you book a call, because it has the joining link and losing it costs you the call. And the note when your account is opened from a new device, because that is the one that tells you if somebody else is in your account.

We send no marketing email at all, so there is no newsletter to leave.
answers.verified_how: Verified: the email switch gates only the discovery call reminders. The booking confirmation is transactional. The new-device notice respects the login_notifications preference, which is on by default.

answers.question: Can I replay the tour later?
answers.answer:
Yes, any time.

Go to Profile and find Product tour under Preferences, then click Replay tour.

The tour walks you through the whole app in 14 short steps. It starts at your Compass and covers each section.

You do not have to finish it. There is a Skip button on every step, and you can stop whenever you like.
answers.verified_how: Walked: the Replay tour control sits under Preferences on the Profile page and restarts the 14-step guided tour.

answers.question: Does reduced motion change anything besides animations?
answers.answer:
Yes, a little more than the name suggests.

When you turn it on, Ally stops almost all movement. Things that used to slide, fade or pop will just appear. Long smooth scrolling stops too, so pages jump straight to where you asked to go.

Nothing is hidden and nothing stops working. You can still reach every page and every button. Only the movement changes.

Ally also follows your device setting. If you have turned on 'Reduce motion' on your phone or computer, Ally is already calm and you do not need this switch.
answers.verified_how: Tested live earlier in this workstream: turning it on flattened 452 animated elements and turning it off restored them. The device's own preference is honoured on load.

answers.question: Can I make the text bigger?
answers.answer:
Use your browser's zoom. On Windows hold Ctrl and press the plus key, and on a Mac hold Command and press plus. Ctrl or Command with zero puts it back.

That scales the whole page, and Ally is built to reflow properly when you do, so nothing runs off the side.

Being straight with you: your browser's separate "text size only" setting will not do much in Ally at the moment. Most of our text is set at a fixed size, so that control mostly passes it by. Zoom is the one that works.

We know, and it is on our list.
answers.verified_how: Measured: of 107 sampled elements, only 7 changed when the root font size was doubled. The app is almost entirely px-based, so text-only scaling has little effect. Page zoom scales everything and the layout reflows without overflow.
answers.finding: Text-only scaling is close to a no-op because the styling is px-based throughout. Not a blocker, but it is an accessibility gap and the answer admits it rather than dodging.

answers.question: Does this work with a screen reader, or by keyboard only?
answers.answer:
Mostly yes, and we have just made one part better.

Every page has a proper heading, a skip link so you can jump past the menu, labels on every field, and descriptions on every image. You can move through the app with the Tab key and use buttons with Enter or Space.

Until today the four switches on your Profile were announced as just "button", with no name and no on-or-off state. That is fixed. They now say what they are and whether they are on.

We have not had Ally formally tested for accessibility. If something does not work for you, please tell us and we will fix it.
answers.verified_how: Audited the Profile page live: 1 main, 1 nav, 1 h1, a skip link present, zero images without alt, zero unlabelled form fields. The only failures were the four switches, fixed in this session and re-verified -- the page now reports zero unnamed controls.
answers.note: Deliberately does not claim WCAG conformance. Nothing has been formally audited, so the answer says what was checked and admits what was not.

answers.question: Is there a dark mode?
answers.answer:
Not yet. Ally is light only at the moment.

If you have your phone or computer set to dark, Ally will not follow it. There is no switch hidden anywhere either, so you are not missing it.

What we do have is reduced motion, under Preferences on your Profile, which helps if the movement rather than the brightness is the problem.

Quite a few people have asked for dark mode. If you would use it, tell us on the Feedback page. It genuinely helps us decide what to build next.
answers.verified_how: Confirmed: zero prefers-color-scheme colour rules are loaded on the app's pages, and the root element carries no data-theme. There is no dark stylesheet to switch to.

answers.question: What's the difference between "download my data" and "export for portability"?
answers.answer:
They give you two different files.

"Download my data" gives you everything we hold. That includes what Ally worked out about you -- your reports, the root causes it found, and what it remembers about your business.

"Export for portability" gives you only what you gave us. Your answers, your goals, your tasks, your conversations and your profile. It leaves out Ally's own analysis, because that is the part you would not be taking anywhere else.

Both are JSON files, both download straight away, and both are in Profile, then Privacy Center.

If you just want a copy of everything, use the first one.
answers.verified_how: Ran both: access returns 23 sections and 183 records; portability returns 11 sections and 126 records, covering only founder-supplied data.

answers.question: What does "view data summary" show me?
answers.answer:
It shows how much we hold, not what it says.

You get counts, grouped into six plain headings: your profile and settings, your diagnosis, your reports and what Ally worked out, your conversations, your goals and tasks, and your account record.

It appears on screen. Nothing downloads, and nothing changes.

It is meant as a quick look before you decide whether to download the full thing. If you want to read the actual data, use "Download my data" on the same page.
answers.verified_how: Ran it: 186 records grouped into six categories plus a catch-all, and the categories reconcile to the total so a new kind of record cannot quietly go missing.

answers.question: I want a fact corrected. Will that change my report?
answers.answer:
We will correct the fact. Your report will not change.

Use "Request data correction" in the Privacy Center and tell us what is wrong and what it should say. A person reads it and fixes the record.

Your report is different. It was written from your answers on the day you did the diagnosis, and it stays as it was -- a record of that moment, not a live document. Correcting a fact now does not rewrite it, and we will not pretend it does.

If the fact was central to what Ally concluded, say so in the request. That is worth a conversation rather than a correction.
answers.verified_how: 'Request data correction' is the one Privacy Center action that queues for a human. Reports are immutable once generated -- nothing anywhere regenerates one, consistent with answer 69.

answers.question: What does "restrict data processing" stop, exactly?
answers.answer:
It stops Ally thinking about you, and nothing else.

While it is on, you cannot send messages to Ally or start a diagnosis. Both stop with a notice telling you to resume from the Privacy Center.

Everything you already have stays exactly as it is. Your account is active, your report is readable, your goals and tasks are all there, and nothing is deleted.

It is a pause, not a decision. You can turn it back on whenever you like and it takes effect straight away.
answers.verified_how: Tested live: with processing restricted, a chat message returns a clear refusal naming the Privacy Center. Nothing stored is affected and resuming restores normal function immediately.

answers.question: What's the difference between restricting processing and withdrawing consent?
answers.answer:
One is a pause. The other is a decision.

Restricting processing is a switch. Ally stops analysing anything new until you turn it back on. Use it if you want a break, or you are thinking something over.

Withdrawing consent takes away our permission to analyse your data at all. It is the formal version, and it is your right under the law.

In practice they stop the same things: no new chat, no new diagnosis. Neither deletes anything, and neither closes your account.

If you are unsure which you want, restrict processing. It is the reversible one.
answers.verified_how: Both surface in the Privacy Center and both block the same two operations. Neither deletes anything or deactivates the account. The right to withdraw consent is section 7(e) of the published Privacy Policy.

answers.question: If I withdraw consent, do I lose my report?
answers.answer:
No. Your report stays and you can still read it.

Withdrawing consent stops new analysis. It does not delete anything you already have. Your report, your Founder DNA, your goals and your past conversations are all still there.

What stops is Ally doing anything new with your data -- no new messages, no new diagnosis.

If you want the report gone as well, that is account deletion, which is a separate action on the same page and has a 30-day window before it becomes permanent.

And if you change your mind, you can give consent again.
answers.verified_how: Withdrawing consent revokes the basis for new processing and leaves every existing record intact. Deletion is a separate action with its own 30-day grace window.

answers.question: I paused processing. How do I start it again?
answers.answer:
Go to Profile, then Privacy Center. There is an amber banner at the top with a Resume button.

Press it and Ally starts working normally again straight away. There is no waiting and nothing to confirm.

If you cannot see the banner, you are probably not paused any more -- try sending Ally a message and see whether it answers.
answers.verified_how: Tested live: the amber banner carries a Resume control and lifting the restriction restores chat and diagnosis immediately.

answers.question: I scheduled deletion by mistake. Can I stop it?
answers.answer:
Yes, and you can do it yourself. Just sign in.

While your deletion is scheduled, signing in shows you a message about it with a button that says "Cancel deletion & continue". Press that and your account carries on as normal.

Nothing has been erased in the meantime. The 30-day window exists precisely so a mis-click is recoverable.

You do not need to email anybody. If the button does not work for you, then write to us -- but it should.
answers.verified_how: Verified: DeletionPendingGate is mounted in PlatformLayout and shows a blocking prompt with a one-click 'Cancel deletion & continue' during the grace window.
answers.note: The question bank recorded this as 'no self-serve cancel, the banner says contact support'. That was true of the COPY, which has since been corrected -- the button itself has existed throughout.

answers.question: How long do I have to change my mind?
answers.answer:
Thirty days from the day you ask for deletion.

Until that date your account works completely normally and nothing has been removed. Sign in any time before it and you will be offered the chance to cancel.

After that date it is permanent. Your data is erased or made anonymous, and it cannot be brought back.

Two things outlive it, and only because the law requires it: financial records are kept for seven years, and anything already made anonymous -- which cannot be traced back to you -- may be kept.

If you want a copy of anything, download it before the date.
answers.verified_how: Matches the published Privacy Policy section 6 word for word: erasure or anonymisation within 30 days, financial records retained 7 years under Indian law, anonymised data retained indefinitely.

answers.question: Is Ally actually DPDP and GDPR compliant, or just saying so?
answers.answer:
DPDP yes. GDPR does not apply to us, and we would rather say so than imply it.

Our Privacy Policy is written to India's Digital Personal Data Protection Act 2023 and the IT Act 2000. That is not just a sentence: the rights it gives you are built and working. You can download your data, export it, ask for a correction, pause processing, withdraw consent and delete your account, all from the Privacy Center, and most happen immediately.

We also name a Grievance Officer, which the DPDP Act requires.

Ally is for founders in India at the moment, which is why GDPR is not something we claim.

We have not been independently audited. If you need that for a compliance review, ask us and we will tell you exactly where we stand.
answers.verified_how: Team decision 2026-09-06: DPDP only, and users are India-based for now, so GDPR is deliberately out of scope. Privacy Policy claims DPDP 2023 and IT Act 2000 and names a Grievance Officer. Every right listed was exercised during the walk.
answers.note: Team decision, 2026-09-06.

answers.question: You say requests are reviewed within 30 days. Why does it take that long?
answers.answer:
For most things it does not. Thirty days is the legal maximum, not our normal speed.

Downloading your data, exporting it, viewing the summary, pausing processing and withdrawing consent all happen the moment you press the button. Nothing waits for anybody.

The one that genuinely needs a person is a data correction, because somebody has to check what is wrong and fix the right record. Those are usually done in a few days.

The thirty days is there so that a hard request, or one that arrives while somebody is away, still has a promise attached to it.
answers.verified_how: Walked all seven Privacy Center actions: six are served immediately, and only 'Request data correction' queues for a human.

answers.question: Who owns my report -- me, or GoXL?
answers.answer:
The contents are yours. The format is ours.

Everything you put in -- your answers, your business information, what you told Ally -- you own outright. Our terms say so plainly, and we only get permission to use it to run the service for you.

What belongs to us is the thing around it: the framework, the way the report is laid out, and the platform itself.

In practice this matters less than it sounds. It is your report, you can download it, keep it and read it forever. If you want to use it in something you are sending outside your business, see the next answer.
answers.verified_how: Terms section 4 ('You retain full ownership of all business information, diagnostic inputs, and data you provide') read against section 6 (the Platform, its models, report formats and design are GoXL's property).

answers.question: Can I use what Ally gives me commercially -- in a pitch, in an investor deck?
answers.answer:
Yes. It is your report and your business -- use it however you like.

Put it in an investor deck, take it into a board meeting, share the whole thing or a single page. That is your call, and we are not going to tell you what to do with a document about your own company.

One practical thought rather than a rule: a report reads as a report. In a deck it usually lands better if you take the finding and put it in your own words and your own slides. But that is a presentation opinion, not a restriction.
answers.verified_how: Team decision 2026-09-06: a founder's use of their own report is their personal choice. Terms section 4 already gives the founder full ownership of their business information and diagnostic inputs.
answers.note: Team decision, 2026-09-06. Earlier drafts hedged on Terms section 6's 'internal business purposes only'. The team's position is that the report is the founder's to use, so the hedge is gone.

answers.question: Can I quote Ally's report to a client of mine?
answers.answer:
Yes, go ahead.

The findings are about your business, so quoting them to a client is entirely your call. Share a line, a section, or the whole report if it helps.

The one thing that is different is reselling. Using Ally as part of a service you charge clients for -- running diagnoses for them, packaging the reports as your own product -- needs a conversation with us first. That is not a no, it just is not automatic.

Write to info@goxl.in if that is what you have in mind.
answers.verified_how: Team decision 2026-09-06. Terms section 5(f) still prohibits reselling or sublicensing access without prior written consent, which is a different thing from a founder quoting their own report.
answers.note: Team decision, 2026-09-06.

answers.question: What are you allowed to do with what I write?
answers.answer:
Use it to run Ally for you, and to make Ally better in a way that is not about you.

Our terms give us a limited licence to process your data solely to deliver the service -- to build your report, to let Ally answer you properly, and to keep your account working.

We do not sell it. We do not rent it. We do not share it with anyone for advertising or marketing.

We also use anonymous, combined information -- patterns across many founders, with nothing that could point back to you -- to improve Ally. Your own writing is never used to train anything, and is never in any searchable index.

It is all in the Terms if you want the full wording.
answers.verified_how: Terms section 4. The aggregate half is the team's settled position as of 2026-09-05 and matches Privacy Policy sections 3(c) and 6. Consistent with answer 206.
answers.note: Team decision, 2026-09-05.

answers.question: Can you close my account? On what grounds?
answers.answer:
We can, and the grounds are in our terms rather than at our whim.

The short version: breaking the rules. Trying to get into someone else's account, deliberately giving false business information, scraping or reverse-engineering the platform, reselling access, or using Ally for something unlawful.

We are not going to close your account for disagreeing with your report, complaining, or asking for a refund.

If we ever did suspend an account, you would be able to ask why and get a straight answer at info@goxl.in.

In practice this has not happened, and the clause exists for the obvious cases rather than the borderline ones.
answers.verified_how: Terms section 3 (suspend or terminate accounts that violate the Terms) and section 5 (the list of prohibited conduct). Section 8 covers termination and what survives it.

answers.question: What happens to my report if GoXL shuts down or gets bought?
answers.verified_how: Retired by team decision 2026-09-06.
answers.note: RETIRED, not unanswered. The team's position is that this is not a question to put in front of founders at launch. It stays in the bank with its id so nobody re-adds it by accident, and is excluded from the export. If a founder does ask, support answers it individually.

answers.question: You changed the terms. Do I have to accept?
answers.answer:
Not by signing anything. Carrying on using Ally is what counts as accepting.

When something important changes, we tell you -- through the app or by email -- before it takes effect. For the Privacy Policy that is at least seven days' notice.

If you are not happy with a change, the honest options are to tell us, or to stop using Ally and delete your account. There is no way to stay on the old terms.

The date and version are always at the top of the Terms page, so you can see what you are on.
answers.verified_how: Terms section 10 (material changes notified via the Platform or email; continued use constitutes acceptance; version and effective date shown at the top). Privacy Policy section 11 specifies at least 7 days' notice.

answers.question: Is there a minimum age?
answers.answer:
Yes. You need to be at least 18.

Our terms require it, and you also have to be able to enter into an agreement for yourself or for your business.

There is no separate account type for anyone younger, and no plans for one.
answers.verified_how: Terms section 1: at least 18 years old, with the legal authority to enter the agreement.

answers.question: If something goes wrong, whose law applies and where?
answers.answer:
Indian law, and the courts in Bangalore.

Our terms say any dispute is governed by the laws of India, and that the courts of Bangalore, Karnataka have exclusive jurisdiction.

Before anything reaches a court, both sides are expected to try to sort it out properly first. If it is still unresolved after 30 days, then it can go further.

For anything short of that -- a complaint, a bill you think is wrong, a report you are unhappy with -- write to info@goxl.in. Almost everything is settled there.
answers.verified_how: Terms section 9: governed by the laws of India, good-faith negotiation first, exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of Bangalore, Karnataka if unresolved within 30 days.

answers.question: Can I rely on Ally's advice? Are you liable if it's wrong?
answers.answer:
Use it to think with. Do not use it as professional advice, and the decision stays yours.

Our terms are direct about this: Ally is a decision-support tool, not legal, financial or management consulting advice, and you remain responsible for what you decide.

On liability, they are equally direct. Ally is provided as is, with no guarantee that everything it produces is accurate, and if you ever did have a claim against us it is capped at what you have paid us in the previous three months.

We would rather you knew that up front than found it in a clause later.

If Ally gets something wrong about your business, please tell us. That is worth fixing.
answers.verified_how: Terms section 2 (decision-support tool, not professional advice, founder solely responsible) and section 7 (AS IS, no warranties as to accuracy, liability capped at three months' fees, no indirect damages).

answers.question: Can I upload my business plan or deck instead of answering all this?
answers.answer:
No. Every question in the diagnosis has to be answered by you.

That is deliberate, and it is the whole point. Ally is trying to understand you, not just your business -- how you describe things, what you reach for first, where you hesitate. A document tells us about the company. It does not tell us about the founder, and half of what the diagnosis reads is the founder.

Your plan is still useful, though. Upload it in a conversation and Ally will work through it with you, quote your own numbers back and tell you what it makes of them.

The diagnosis takes about half an hour, and you can stop and come back.
answers.verified_how: Team decision 2026-09-05: the diagnosis will not be pre-filled or shortened from an uploaded document, because the system needs to hear from the founder directly. Chat file reading is unaffected and still works for PDFs, Word, plain text and CSV.
answers.note: Team decision, 2026-09-05.

answers.question: Can Ally connect to my accounting, CRM or bank data?
answers.answer:
No, and there is no plan to connect to your bank.

Ally works from what you tell it, not from your systems. Nothing is plugged into your accounts.

For what it does, that matters less than you would think. The diagnosis asks for rough figures -- roughly what is coming in, roughly how many customers -- and approximate answers are genuinely fine.

If you want Ally to look at real numbers, export them and upload the file in a conversation. It reads spreadsheets and PDFs, and it can work through your actual figures with you that way.

If a particular connection would change things for you, tell us which one.
answers.verified_how: Searched the whole repo: no accounting, CRM or banking integration exists. CSV upload in chat is real and was tested -- Ally quoted exact figures from an uploaded file.

answers.question: Does it work with Notion, Slack, or anything I already use?
answers.answer:
Not yet. Ally does not connect to Notion, Slack or any other tool.

The one exception is your calendar. Connect it from Plan Your Day and your tasks go into it, so at least the things you decide to do turn up where you already look.

Everything else is copy and paste for now. Your report downloads as a PDF, so it goes into Notion or a Drive folder easily enough.

If there is one tool you would genuinely use this with, tell us which. We are keeping a list, and it is short enough that a few votes decide it.
answers.verified_how: Google Calendar is the only outbound integration in the product. No Notion, Slack or Zapier code exists anywhere.

answers.question: Is there an API?
answers.answer:
No. There is no public API and nothing you can build against.

Ally's data moves in and out two ways: your report downloads as a PDF, and the Privacy Center gives you a full JSON export of everything we hold, which is machine-readable if you want to do something with it.

For most people that export is the thing they actually wanted.

If you have a real use for an API, please tell us what you would do with it. That is the sort of thing we would build for a reason and not on spec.
answers.verified_how: There is no public API surface, no founder-facing API key and no developer documentation. The privacy export is genuine machine-readable JSON.
answers.note: Deliberately does NOT say 'not yet'. An API is a long-term commitment to a contract, and 'not yet' from a support bot is how a roadmap promise gets made by accident.

answers.question: Can I bring my existing goals in from another tool?
answers.answer:
Not automatically. There is no import.

You would need to type them in on the Goals page, which is genuinely quick for the handful that matter.

And honestly, that is not the worst thing. Most founders arrive with a list of twenty goals from somewhere else, and the useful exercise is deciding which three are real. Ally is built around a small number of things you are actually going to do.

If you are moving from another tool and have a long list, bring it to a conversation with Ally and work out which ones to keep.
answers.verified_how: No import path exists for goals or tasks. Goals are created in Ally or come out of the diagnosis.

answers.question: Can I refer another founder? Do I get anything for it?
answers.answer:
Please do tell them about us -- but there is no referral scheme, so there is nothing in it for you at the moment. No code to share, no credit, no discount.

What there is: our first 100 founders get benefits and coupons as a thank-you for being early. If you are one of them, that comes to you automatically -- there is nothing to claim.

If a proper referral scheme would make you tell more people, say so. That is the kind of thing that gets built when enough people ask.
answers.verified_how: Team decision 2026-09-06: no referral programme; the first 100 users receive benefits and coupons instead. Confirmed that nothing in the repo implements referrals.
answers.finding: The first-100 benefit is a promise with no mechanism behind it yet. Nothing in the catalog or the credits system grants anything to early founders automatically. Somebody needs to decide what they get and how it is applied before the 100th signup, not after.
answers.note: Team decision, 2026-09-06.

answers.question: I'm a nonprofit / an agency / a one-person practice. Does the model still apply?
answers.answer:
Mostly yes, with one honest caveat.

Ally is built around a founder and the organisation they are running. That much fits a nonprofit, an agency or a practice of one as well as it fits a startup. The questions about clarity, focus, what only you can decide and what is actually stuck are the same questions.

The caveat is revenue. Some of what Ally looks at assumes money coming from customers. If you are grant-funded, or your income works differently, that part will fit less well and the report will be thinner there.

Everything about you as the person running it applies exactly the same.
answers.verified_how: The framework is stage-and-business based. Revenue Maturity is one of six pillars and is scoped out at early stages, so a founder without conventional revenue gets a report weighted to the other five rather than a broken one.

answers.question: My cofounder reads the business completely differently. Can Ally handle that?
answers.answer:
Not in one account, no. Ally hears one voice -- whoever answered the questions.

So the report reflects how you see the business. If your cofounder would have answered differently, that difference does not appear anywhere, and the report is not the neutral referee between you.

There are two things worth doing. Read the report together and mark where they would have answered differently -- that disagreement is usually more useful than the report itself. And bring it to a discovery call, where a person can hold both readings at once.

A proper two-founder version does not exist yet.
answers.verified_how: One diagnosis per account, answered by one founder. There is no multi-user account, no cofounder access and no way to record a second set of answers. Consistent with answers 31, 200 and 201.

answers.question: Does this work on slow or patchy internet?
answers.answer:
Mostly, but it will feel slow in two places.

Ally's replies arrive a piece at a time, so on a weak connection they come in slowly rather than failing. That part copes.

The two heavy moments are your Compass, which loads a lot at once, and downloading your report as a PDF.

If a page does not load, refreshing usually fixes it. Nothing is lost when a connection drops -- your diagnosis answers are saved one at a time as you send them, so you never go back to the beginning.
answers.verified_how: Answers are persisted individually on submit, so a dropped connection costs at most the answer in flight. Compass is the heaviest page in the product and the report PDF is the largest single download.

answers.question: Does any of it work offline?
answers.answer:
No. Ally needs a connection for everything.

There is nothing stored on your device to fall back on, so with no internet you will not be able to open it at all.

The one thing you can keep offline is your report. Download it as a PDF and it is yours to read on a plane or anywhere else.

If you know you are going to be without a connection, download it first.
answers.verified_how: No service worker and no PWA manifest exist, so there is no offline capability of any kind. The report PDF is the only artefact a founder can keep locally.

answers.question: Everything is in rupees and Indian examples. Does it hold up for a business abroad?
answers.answer:
The thinking does. The furniture around it is Indian.

What Ally actually measures -- your clarity, your market, how your revenue works, whether too much depends on you -- is not specific to any country. A founder in Berlin gets the same six areas and the same kind of root cause.

What is Indian is the surroundings. Prices are in rupees, support runs on India time, and the case studies behind the framework are Indian businesses. So some examples will feel local.

Nothing checks where you are, so it works wherever you sit. If you are outside India and thinking of paying, write to us first.
answers.verified_how: Nothing in the scoring, the six pillars or the root-cause rules is geography-dependent. Prices are INR, support hours are IST, and the knowledge base was built from Indian founder case studies. Consistent with answer 234.
